English: For the couple too, the words <tips=17>Type B</tips> brought dramatic symptoms immediately to mind, so they were afraid from the outset. When they actually saw their daughter possessed by delusions and shouting incomprehensible things, that fear only intensified.

English: Overpowering psychotropic medication left her dazed all day and scarcely capable of conversation. She muttered under her breath and smiled faintly to herself. She could no longer even write.

English: Then one night, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> rose abruptly and set fire to the family home. Fortunately, everyone escaped, but the family dog died, and her younger sister suffered burns that left permanent scars.

English: Her mother wept as she struck <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> across the cheek with all her strength.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は混乱し、泣きわめく。
English: Bewildered, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> wailed.

Japanese: 「やめてよ！　偽物のくせに！　本当のお母さんを返してっ！」

English: The arson was born of her delusion. Convinced that her family had been replaced by impostors, she had set the fire in the belief that if she burned them, her real family would come back.

English: Once she had caused an incident like this, she could no longer live in society.

Japanese: これがきっかけに彼女は半ば強制的に入院させられることになり、やがて症状がさらに悪化すると特に重度のものが収容される<tips=6>巻河原病院</tips>へ転院することとなった。
English: The incident led to her being hospitalized against her will in all but name. When her condition deteriorated still further, she was eventually transferred to <tips=6>Makigawara Hospital</tips>, an institution reserved for especially severe cases.

English: Her parents did not know that this was an infamous institution known as the “<tips=6>Type B Internment Center</tips>.”

Japanese: それから三年間、<tips=9>Y地区</tips>の外れにあるこの古びた建物のなかで、<tips=82>内田広美</tips>は十代の貴重な時間を過ごした。
English: For the next three years, <tips=82>Hiromi Uchida</tips> spent precious years of her adolescence inside that aging building on the outskirts of <tips=9>Y District</tips>.

Japanese: 若さのわりにあまりにも症状の進行が早く、人格は完全に崩壊し、自分の身のまわりのことは排泄や入浴さえ介助がなければまともに出来ず、ほとんど誰とも会話を成立させることが出来なかった。
English: Her illness had progressed with extraordinary speed for someone so young. Her personality had completely disintegrated; without assistance, she could not properly manage even her own toileting or bathing, and she could scarcely carry on a coherent conversation with anyone.

Japanese: それが、病院を襲撃した<tips=21>八龍会</tips><tips=47>解放軍</tips>に『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』を投与された途端、にわかに年相応の心と理性を取り戻したのである。
English: All that changed the moment the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> that had attacked the hospital administered <tips=46>Neo Rose</tips> to her: she suddenly regained the mind and reason of someone her age.

English: For some time, she could not comprehend the miracle that had befallen her.

English: The delusions and hallucinations that had filled her mind receded, allowing her to see reality as it was. The first thing she sensed was the choking smell of blood.

Japanese: 彼女はホールの片隅の壁に寄りかかって座り込んでいた。その向こうには、白衣の人々の折り重なった死体があり、そこから流れ出る真っ赤な血液が小さな池を作っている。
English: She sat in one corner of the hall with her back against the wall. Beyond her lay a heap of bodies in white coats, and the vivid red blood flowing from them had formed a small pool.

English: Most of the faces were familiar to her.

Japanese: 症状に冒されていた間の記憶は、全く失われたわけじゃない。彼らと会話したり、一緒に遊んだことは覚えている。それがこうして変わり果てた姿になり、かわりに銃を持ったいかめしい顔つきの人々が闊歩している。
English: Her memories of the time her symptoms had consumed her were not entirely gone. She remembered talking and playing with these people. Now here they were, reduced to this terrible state, while grim-faced people carrying guns strode about in their place.

English: The sight was so dreamlike that it took her some time to understand that her delusions had left her and she had returned to reality.

Japanese: 自分の手を握ったり開いたりして、ぼんやりとそれを眺めている。
English: She opened and closed her hands, staring at them vaguely.

Japanese: （ぐー。ぱー。ぐー。ぱー……）
English: (Clench. Open. Clench. Open...)

English: As she repeated the words inside her head, she gazed at the neatly trimmed nails on those slender white fingers. They had been cut only the day before yesterday by Miyako Norita, the nursing assistant who now lay among the corpses before her.

Japanese: （ぐー。ぱー。ぐー。ぱー……）
English: (Clench. Open. Clench. Open...)

Japanese: うつろな表情で握ったり開いたりを繰り返していると、３０８号室の方から男の荒々しい怒鳴り声が聞こえて来る。
English: As she continued opening and closing her hands with a vacant expression, a man’s furious shout came from the direction of Room 308.

Japanese: <tips=47>解放軍</tips>の男が、患者たちに集まるよう呼びかけている。
English: A <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> man was calling for the patients to gather.

Japanese: 長年の病院暮らしですっかり従順になっていた<tips=82>広美</tips>は、その言葉によってほとんど自動的に立ち上がると、夢遊病者のような足取りで声の方向へ向かった。
English: Long years in the hospital had made <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> completely obedient. At his words, she rose almost automatically and moved toward the voice with the steps of a sleepwalker.

Japanese: 畳敷きのその大部屋には<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>の効果によって本来の人格と知性を取り戻し、<tips=82>広美</tips>が知っているものとは違うきりりとした顔つきになった患者たちが集まり、不安げな表情で口々に何かを囁きあっている。<tips=82>広美</tips>はその端のほうにちょこんと正座をした。
English: Patients had gathered in the large tatami room, their original personalities and intellects restored by <tips=46>Neo Rose</tips>. Their alert, composed faces bore little resemblance to the ones <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> knew, and they exchanged anxious whispers. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> tucked herself into seiza at the very edge of the group.

Japanese: 前には銃を持った<tips=47>解放軍</tips>のメンバーが立っている。そしてそのなかでただ一人の女性が話し始めた。
English: <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> members carrying guns stood before them. The only woman among them began to speak.

Japanese: 彼女はまず副隊長の<tips=67>カミラ・ノーサム</tips>と名乗った。
English: She began by introducing herself as Deputy Commander <tips=67>Camilla Northam</tips>.

Japanese: 「我々は<tips=47>八龍解放軍</tips>です。あなたたちをこの恐ろしい場所から解放するためにやって来ました」
English: “We are the <tips=47>Hachiryu Liberation Army</tips>. We have come to liberate you from this horrific place.”

English: In a clear, ringing voice, <tips=67>Camilla</tips> proclaimed the purpose of their organization.

English: Curious how the other patients were receiving these words, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> stole glances at their faces.

English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> understood the words themselves, but Camilla’s passionate delivery failed to resonate with her. If anything, she found it somehow frightening.

English: There were many elderly people in the group. Some clung to the railing and trembled as they descended the stairs. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> supported one woman by the shoulder and went down beside her.

English: She whispers into <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> ear so the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> members ahead cannot hear.

Japanese: 病棟から出た<tips=82>広美</tips>が見た光景は、曇天からとめどもなく降り落ちる雨だった。迂闊に一歩を踏み出すと、介護シューズを履いた足がぬかるんだ泥を踏み、中に水が沁みた。
English: When <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> emerged from the ward, she found rain streaming without end from an overcast sky. She took an unwary step. Her care shoe sank into the mud, and water seeped inside.

English: They passed through the gate in the rain, their feet coated with mud. The world beyond it was one most of the patients had not entered for years—and some, for decades.

English: But they had no time to savor the moment. Four minibuses waited beside the exit, and the patients were instructed to board them.

English: The operation appeared pressed for time. As the group, composed mostly of elderly people, shuffled slowly aboard, the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> men shouted, ‘Too slow!’ and ‘Hurry up!’

Japanese: 「細井さんは、お子さんに会わないんですか？」
English: “Aren’t you going to see your child, Ms. Hosoi?”

Japanese: 「ああ、子供ね……」
English: “Oh. My child...”

Japanese: 細井は言葉を濁す。そして、彼女の布団の方から、もぞもぞと動くような音が聞こえた。
English: Hosoi evades the question. From her futon comes the rustle of her shifting beneath the covers.

Japanese: 彼女は病院でいつも子供の幻覚を見ていた。誰もいない廊下を大きくなった娘が走っていると言ったり、その日は誰とも面会などしていないのに娘が会いに来たと言ったり。職員が誰も来ていないと説明すると、顔を真っ赤にして金切り声を上げていた。
English: At the hospital, she was forever seeing visions of her child. She would say that her grown daughter was running down an empty corridor, or that her daughter had come to visit on a day when no one had visited her at all. When the staff explained that no one had come, her face would turn scarlet and she would shriek at them.

Japanese: 症状によって外界の情報には疎いまま過ごしていた<tips=82>広美</tips>にも、繰り返されるその言葉を聞いた覚えがある。
English: Even <tips=82>Hiromi</tips>, who had passed those years cut off from outside information by her symptoms, remembers hearing those repeated claims.

Japanese: 「産んだのよ。本当に産んで、子供はいるの。……でも、見た覚えがないの。男か女かもしらない」
English: “I gave birth. I truly did. I have a child... But I don’t remember seeing the baby. I don’t even know whether it was a boy or a girl.”

Japanese: 「どうして……」
English: “Why not...?”

Japanese: 「その頃私はもうおかしくなりかかってて、抱かせて貰えなかった。出産後にすぐに<tips=17>タイプB</tips>用の病院に行くことになって……今はどうしているのかもわからないわ。もしかしたら施設にでも入れたのかもしれない」
English: “I was already beginning to lose my mind by then, so they wouldn’t let me hold the baby. Immediately after giving birth, I was sent to a hospital for <tips=17>Type Bs</tips>... I don’t know where the child is now. Perhaps they placed it in some institution.”

Japanese: 「……お父さんは？」
English: “...What about the father?”

Japanese: 「それも誰だかわからない。それっぽい人は何人かいるけど」
English: “I don’t know who he is either. There are several men it might have been.”

Japanese: 細井は乾いた声で笑った。
English: Hosoi laughs dryly.

Japanese: 「だから会いたいけど、会えないわ。きっと私の親はどうなったか教えてくれないし……それに、今更どんな顔をして会えばいいかわからないもの」
English: “So I want to meet the child, but I can’t. My parents would never tell me what happened... And after all this time, I have no idea how I could face the child.”

Japanese: その暗い声色に<tips=82>広美</tips>は戸惑った。<tips=82>広美</tips>からすれば、会いたいのなら会えばいいのではないかと単純にそう思う。さっきバスのなかでいろいろと言われたが、いまひとつピンと来なかった。確かに昔は病気だったからいろいろと迷惑をかけたこともあるかもしれないが、今はもう完全に元に戻ったのだ。その姿を見せればいいはずだ。
English: The darkness in her voice leaves <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> perplexed. From <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> perspective, if Hosoi wants to see the child, she should simply do so. People had told her all sorts of things on the bus earlier, but none of it had quite sunk in. It was true that she had been ill and might have caused everyone a great deal of trouble. But now she was completely back to normal. Surely all she had to do was let them see her as she was now.

Japanese: だが、大人は大人で少し事情が違うのかもしれない。
English: Perhaps circumstances are a little different for adults.

Japanese: 「だから私はしばらくここにいるわ。<tips=21>八龍会</tips>ってのに入るかどうかはわからないけど、みんなと一緒の方が気楽に過ごせるかもしれない。長年一緒だし。……でも、変なもんだよね。正直ね、他の患者さんたちって好きじゃなかった。一刻もはやく離れたいと思ったけど、いざこうなるとなんだか一番信用出来るような気がして……。<tips=82>広美</tips>ちゃんのことも面倒な子だって思ってたけど、今はそうでもないわ」
English: “So I’ll stay here for a while. I don’t know whether I’ll join the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>, but perhaps I can relax more easily with everyone else. We were together for years. ...It is strange, though. Honestly, I didn’t like the other patients. I wanted to escape them as soon as possible. But now that this has happened, somehow I feel as though I can trust them more than anyone... I thought you were a difficult child too, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips>, but I don’t feel that way now.”

Japanese: 「そうですか……」
English: “I see...”

Japanese: 「ずっと一緒にいたけれど、こんな風に話したのは初めてだし、なんだかびっくりしちゃった。……ねえ、ご両親の住所がわかっても、すぐに出ていかないで、何日かここで暮らさない？　ブランクがあるから少し世間に慣れてから親御さんと会った方がいいかもしれないし、他の患者さんたちと話して、みんなが本当はどんな人だったのか知るのもいいと思う」
English: “We’ve been together all these years, but this is the first time we’ve ever talked like this. I’m sort of amazed. ...Listen, even when they find your parents’ address, why not stay here for a few days instead of leaving right away? You’ve been out of society for a while, so it might be better to get used to the world again before you see your parents. And I think it would be good to talk to the other patients and find out what everyone was really like.”

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>が横目で細井の方を見ると、彼女は身体ごと向きを変えてこちらの方を見ていた。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> glances toward Hosoi. The other woman has turned her entire body and is looking back at her.

Japanese: 「私、どう受け入れたらいいかわからないんです」
English: “I don’t know how to come to terms with any of it.”

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は正直に口にした。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> answers honestly.

Japanese: 「あの人たちが私たちの病気を治してくれたみたいですけど、あんなに乱暴なことをして……いい人たちなのか、悪い人たちなのかわからなくて……」
English: “Those people seem to have cured our illness, but they did something so violent... I don’t understand whether they’re good people or bad people...”

Japanese: 「ああ、あなた職員に可愛がられてたものねえ。特に担当の<tips=83>能見</tips>さんとか、本当に妹みたいにしてくれてたもんね」
English: “Oh, the staff were fond of you. Especially Ms. <tips=83>Nomi</tips>, your assigned nurse. She truly treated you like a little sister.”

Japanese: 具体的に名前を出されると、<tips=82>広美</tips>の脳裏にあの血みどろのホールの映像が浮かんだ。
English: Hearing the specific name brings the image of that blood-soaked hall back into <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> mind.

Japanese: あの時はぼんやりといていて、はっきりと知覚していなかったが、あらためて思い出して見ると確かにそこには看護師の<tips=83>能見美紗</tips>も倒れていた。
English: She had been dazed then and did not perceive the scene clearly. Looking back upon it now, however, the nurse <tips=83>Misa Nomi</tips> was indeed lying there.

Japanese: 目を見開き、真っ白なナース服を血の赤に染めて。
English: Eyes staring wide, her snow-white nurse’s uniform dyed red with blood.

Japanese: 「覚えてる。あなた、粗相したりいじめられたりすると、泣きながら『ノミさん、ノミさん』って呼んでたのよ？　もう口癖みたいになってて、まーた<tips=82>広美</tips>ちゃんの『ノミさん、ノミさん』がはじまったってみんな笑ってたんだから」
English: “I remember. Whenever you had an accident or someone bullied you, you cried and called, ‘Ms. Nomi, Ms. Nomi.’ It became almost a catchphrase. Everyone used to laugh and say, ‘There goes <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> with her Ms. Nomi, Ms. Nomi again.’”

Japanese: 「あんまり、覚えてないです……」
English: “I don’t remember it very well...”

Japanese: 自分はそんなに甘えていたのか？　<tips=82>広美</tips>は恥ずかしくなって、顔が熱くなるのを感じた。
English: Had she depended upon the woman so completely? <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> grows embarrassed and feels heat gather in her face.

Japanese: 「ま、職員の人たちとのつき合いは長いからね。複雑な気持ちになるのはわかるわ。でも、あれは仕方ないことだったのよ」
English: “Well, we’d known the staff for years. I understand why you have mixed feelings. But there was no helping what happened.”

Japanese: 細井は溜息まじりに言う。
English: Hosoi speaks through a sigh.

Japanese: 「あの<tips=47>解放軍</tips>っていうのは、つまり革命家なのよ。これまでとは違う、全く新しい<tips=17>タイプB</tips>のための社会を作るための革命をしているの。革命には流血がつきものだわ。確かに病院にはいい人も沢山いたし、治りもしない治療をしてたことだって、それは彼らの医学が限界だっただけで、悪気があったわけじゃない。でも、彼らがああいう治療をして、私たちを閉じ込めていたのは今のノーマルの社会を守るためなんだからね。<tips=47>解放軍</tips>はそのノーマルの社会を壊そうとしてるわけだから、<tips=83>能見</tips>さんたちは最初に死ななくちゃいけなかったの」
English: “The <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips>—they’re revolutionaries, in other words. They’re carrying out a revolution to create a completely new society for <tips=17>Type Bs</tips>, unlike anything that came before. Revolutions always entail bloodshed. There certainly were many good people at the hospital. Even when they gave us treatments that could never cure us, it was only because their medicine had reached its limits. They meant no harm. But the reason they treated us that way and kept us confined was to protect today’s Normal society. The <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> is trying to destroy that Normal society, so Ms. <tips=83>Nomi</tips> and the others had to be the first to die.”

Japanese: 「……細井さんは、頭がいいんですね」
English: “...You’re very intelligent, Ms. Hosoi.”

Japanese: 「ちゃんと学校出たんだから。短大だけど」
English: “I did graduate from school. It was only a junior college.”

Japanese: 細井は自嘲するように笑ったが、<tips=82>広美</tips>にはその笑いの意味がわからなかった。
English: Hosoi gives a self-deprecating laugh. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> does not understand its meaning.

Japanese: そして翌朝、患者たちは部屋に運ばれた弁当で朝食をとったあと、近くの公民館のような場所に集められて改めて説明が行われた。
English: The next morning, after eating bento delivered to their rooms, the patients are gathered inside a nearby building resembling a community hall and given another explanation.

Japanese: 『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』の効果や、その使い方が実物を使って話され、そしてその薬が今どうやって作られているのか。リーと名乗ったその人の良さそうな人物の中国語なまりの男の言葉によれば、地域内のあちこちのアパートや民家が工場となり、<tips=21>八龍会</tips>のメンバーが製造やパッケージ詰めをしているという。機械は家庭用製材機を用いた簡単なもので、患者のうち行き場がなくここで働きたいというものは、この作業に参加することになるだろうということだった。
English: They are shown the actual drug while its effects and the use of <tips=46>Neo Rose</tips> are explained, followed by an account of how it is now produced. According to the amiable-looking man with a Chinese accent who introduces himself as Lee, apartments and private homes throughout the district have been turned into workshops where members of the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> manufacture and package it. The equipment is simple, consisting of household pharmaceutical compounding machines. Patients with nowhere else to go who wish to work here will apparently take part in the operation.

Japanese: それから患者のこれからの生活のために必要な物品が配布されていた。
English: Next, the patients are issued the things they will need for life from now on.

Japanese: 患者たちは私物のほとんどを病院に置いてきているし、所持金なども決まりによって病院の事務所に預けている。<tips=47>解放軍</tips>は襲撃の時に病院の事務所から略奪を行っていたので、衣服などの私物はともかく、金銭は持ち主の手に戻すことが出来た。
English: They left almost all their personal possessions in the hospital, while rules required them to deposit money with the hospital office. During the attack, the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> looted that office. Although clothing and other possessions could not readily be restored, they were able to return the money to its owners.

Japanese: 何も持たない患者にはいくばくかの小遣いが与えられた。洗面道具などの日用品はアパートの部屋に置かれているもので足りなかったら、その小遣いで賄うか、相談すれば調達してくれるということだった。
English: Patients who possessed nothing receive a little spending money. Toiletries and other daily necessities have been placed in the apartments. If anything is missing, they can buy it with this allowance or request that it be procured.

Japanese: それから、希望者は<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の有志から集められた古着などから選んで持って帰ってよいということで、配布会が行われた。
English: They then held a giveaway where anyone who wished could choose and take home used clothing and other items donated by volunteers from the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>.

Japanese: その日の説明会には<tips=47>解放軍</tips>のものは参加しておらず、<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の通常メンバーがあたっていた。
English: No members of the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> took part in that day’s briefing; ordinary members of the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> handled it instead.

Japanese: 年齢は、二十代から三十代くらいの若者たちで、男もいれば女もおり、肌が黒いものもいれば白いものもいた。
English: They are young people in their twenties and thirties, both men and women, some dark-skinned and some light-skinned.

Japanese: 彼らはみな親切で、症状がなくなったとは言え特殊な環境下で生活したせいか常識にかけるところのある元患者たちの質問や不満にも、丁寧に対応した。
English: All of them are kind. Although their symptoms are gone, years in an unusual environment have left some former patients unfamiliar with ordinary social norms. The Eight Dragons Society members respond patiently even to their questions and complaints.

Japanese: そして<tips=82>広美</tips>には、昨夜細井が予測した通り、この場で家族の住所が伝えられた。
English: And as Hosoi predicted the previous night, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> receives her family’s address there.

Japanese: 「でも、すぐ帰るのはどうかと思うよ」
English: “But I’m not sure you should go home immediately.”

Japanese: 書類を見せてくれた係員の男性がそう首を捻る。
English: The male coordinator showing her the document tilts his head.

Japanese: 「どうしてですか？」
English: “Why not?”
character_cue: 【内田広美（患者のＵ）】 Arg2=金目困惑 Arg3=キャラ最左中

Japanese: 「向こうもびっくりするだろうしね。とりあえずきみはここで生活して、僕たちの方からご家族にうまく説明し、会う約束をとりつけるというのはどうだろう？」
English: “They will be startled too. How would this sound? For now, you live here while we explain the situation properly to your family and arrange a meeting.”

Japanese: 東南アジア系の血でも混ざっているのか、日本人にしてはどことなく顔つきの濃い係員は優しげにそう言った。
English: Perhaps he has some Southeast Asian ancestry; his features are somewhat pronounced for a Japanese man. He speaks gently.

Japanese: 裏があるようには見えないし、<tips=82>広美</tips>としても本心から善意のつもりで言ってくれているのだとは思う。そうわかってはいても、どうにもここに自分を引き留めようとしているように感じられ、<tips=82>広美</tips>の態度は頑なになってしまう。
English: He does not appear to have any ulterior motive, and <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> believes that he is speaking out of sincere goodwill. Even knowing that, she cannot shake the feeling that he is trying to keep her here, and <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> grows obstinate.

Japanese: 「いえ、すぐに行きます。出来れば今日にでも」
English: “No. I’m going at once. Today, if possible.”
character_cue: 【内田広美（患者のＵ）】 Arg2=金目真顔

Japanese: うつむき視線を合わせないまま、はっきりと言い切った。
English: She speaks firmly without raising her face or meeting his eyes.

Japanese: 係員は溜息をつき、結局翌日の朝にここを出発するということで話を進めることになった。
English: The coordinator sighs, and in the end they settle on having Hiromi leave the following morning.

Japanese: 朝の会合が終わると自由行動となるが、ずっと病院で過ごして急に正常な精神と自由を与えられた患者たちは一晩明けた今日となってもみな動揺を隠せなかった。<tips=82>広美</tips>と同じアパートに振り分けられた元患者のうち、その日に家族と連絡が付き、無事街を出ていったのは入院時から比較的症状が軽く、病院生活もまだ浅く、家族と良好な関係を持つ一名だけだった。
English: Once the morning meeting ends, the patients are free to do as they please. Yet after spending so long in the hospital and then abruptly regaining lucid minds and their freedom, they remain visibly unsettled even on this second day. Among the former patients assigned to <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> building, only one contacts her family that day and safely leaves the city. She had experienced relatively mild symptoms even before admission, had spent little time in the hospital, and maintained a good relationship with her family.

Japanese: あとのものはそれぞれ複雑な事情があり、連絡を思いとどまったり、そもそも家族と関わるつもりがないものばかりだった。
English: Everyone else has complicated circumstances of one kind or another. They either think better of making contact or have no intention of dealing with their families at all.

Japanese: 「急に症状がなくなったと言って信じて貰えると思う？　それに、たとえ受け入れてくれたとしても、今まで散々ひどいことを言われたのに、治ったら急に手のひらをかえされたって、いやな気持ちだわ」
English: “Do you really think they’ll believe us if we suddenly announce that our symptoms are gone? And even if they accept me, after all the cruel things they said before, it would only feel horrible if they reversed themselves the moment I was cured.”

Japanese: 田村という五十がらみの人物はその半生のほとんどを病院や施設で過ごして来た人物だが、子供の頃家庭でに弟にいじめられていたことや、面会にほとんど来ない両親のことを恨んでいる。
English: A woman of about fifty named Tamura has spent nearly her entire life in hospitals and institutions. She resents the younger brother who bullied her at home when she was a child, and the parents who almost never visited.

Japanese: 彼女は症状に冒されていた頃は童女のように無邪気でいつも空笑していたが、こうして知性を取り戻すとやたらと愚痴っぽく、陰気な表情で何かの悪口ばかり言うようになっていた。
English: While in the grip of her symptoms, she had been as innocent as a little girl, forever laughing vacantly. Now that her intelligence has returned, she complains incessantly, glowering as she speaks ill of one person or another.

Japanese: 「あの人、病気の時のほうが可愛かったね」
English: “She was cuter when she was sick, wasn’t she?”

Japanese: と細井が<tips=82>広美</tips>に耳打ちした。<tips=82>広美</tips>にしても同感だったけれども、頷くのは残酷に思えて返事が出来なかった。
English: Hosoi whispers this into <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> ear. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> agrees, but it feels cruel to nod, so she cannot answer.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>も含め、多くの重症患者は<tips=21>八龍会</tips>から与えられた薬によって大きく変化していたが、そうでないものもいた。
English: Many of the severe patients, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> among them, had changed dramatically under the medicine provided by the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>. But some had not.

Japanese: <tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>は<tips=17>タイプB</tips>の症状は取り除くが、他の病には効き目がない。年老いて認知症が進行したものや、その他の精神疾患が併発しているものは、以前と変わったようには見えなかった。
English: <tips=46>Neo Rose</tips> removes the symptoms of <tips=17>Type B</tips>, but has no effect upon other illnesses. Elderly patients with advanced dementia and those suffering concurrently from other mental illnesses did not appear any different from before.

Japanese: そういった、治療が必要な人々は<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の人々によってどこかへ連れて行かれた。近くの病院に入院するのだという。
English: People like these who still need treatment are taken somewhere by members of the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>. They are apparently to be admitted to a nearby hospital.

Japanese: <tips=21>八龍会</tips>としては、特にこの先の目的がない人々には、この街に残り、同志として活動をしてほしいようだった。
English: The <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> apparently wants people with no particular plans for what comes next to remain in the city and work as comrades.

Japanese: 当面ここで生活をすることを決めた元患者たちに、近くのスーパーマーケットなどの生活に必要な施設の場所を説明する傍らで、この<tips=9>Y地区</tips>が<tips=17>タイプB</tips>にとっていかに住みやすい場所かを伝え、<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の活動を伝えた。
English: While showing the former patients who have decided to stay for the time being where to find nearby supermarkets and other facilities essential to daily life, the members also tell them how hospitable <tips=9>Y District</tips> is to <tips=17>Type Bs</tips> and promote the work of the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>.

Japanese: 近くでそれを聞いていた<tips=82>広美</tips>は、彼らが目をきらきらと輝かせて語る『<tips=17>タイプB</tips>の解放』だとか『差別のない社会』という言葉にはどうにも興味が持てず、そのために活動をしているという彼らの情熱も理解出来なかった。彼女からすれば、たとえば病院に数多くいた、妄想について楽しそうに語る患者を眺めているのと同じ気分である。美味しいご飯の話をしたり、面白いテレビ番組の話をして楽しくなるのはわかるけれど、彼らの言っていることはわからない。
English: Listening nearby, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> cannot make herself care about phrases such as ‘the liberation of <tips=17>Type Bs</tips>’ and ‘a society without discrimination,’ which make their eyes shine. Nor can she understand their passion for such work. To her, it feels like watching patients at the hospital happily describe their delusions. She can understand growing excited about delicious food or an entertaining television program. She cannot understand what these people are saying.

Japanese: そして、そんなよくわからない理屈のために、あの血みどろの病院の光景を作りだしたり、赤の他人である自分たちを救い出してこのように手厚く保護するという常軌を逸した行動をするのも、なにやら病気じみている。

English: Perhaps the vibrations of the train and the landscape beyond the window stimulate her mind. As if she had opened Pandora’s box, memories of childhood spring forth one after another.

Japanese: めくるめく感情と記憶の奔流にほとんど目眩を感じてくらくらしているうちに、<tips=82>広美</tips>は目指す駅に辿り着いていた。
English: Almost dizzy beneath the dazzling torrent of emotion and memory, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> finds that she has arrived at her destination.

Japanese: 家族は昔<tips=82>広美</tips>が住んでいた頃から引っ越していない。駅前の風景にはところどころ見覚えがあった。
English: Her family has not moved since the days long ago when <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> lived with them. Here and there, the streets around the station look familiar.

Japanese: いつもお菓子を買って貰っていたコンビニエンスストアー。買い物のついでに季節の衣類をよく出していたクリーニング店には、あのころとほとんど変わらないきついパーマのかかった無愛想な女店員が立っている。
English: There is the convenience store where her parents always bought her sweets. At the dry cleaner where they often dropped off seasonal clothing while out shopping, the same unfriendly woman with the tight perm stands behind the counter, looking almost unchanged from those days.

Japanese: はじめは携帯の地図を頼りに歩いていたが、家に近づくにつれてもやがはれるように記憶が鮮明になり、必要がなくなった。
English: At first, Hiromi walks with the map on her phone as a guide. As she approaches her house, however, her memories sharpen as though a fog has lifted, and she no longer needs it.

Japanese: 友だちと泥遊びをした公園の前を通り過ぎ、虫を捕まえた空き地は今はマンションになっていて、その前の角を曲がる。<tips=82>広美</tips>は早足になり、胸の鼓動は興奮で高鳴った。
English: She passes the park where she made mud pies with her friends. The vacant lot where she caught insects has become an apartment building. She turns at the corner beyond it. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> quickens her pace, her heart pounding with excitement.

Japanese: そして、記憶のなかの自分の家の前に辿り着いて立ち止まると、手に握りしめた携帯電話から『目的の場所に到着しました』というアナウンスが流れる。
English: Then she reaches the house from her memories and stops before it. From the phone clenched in her hand comes an announcement: ‘You have arrived at your destination.’

Japanese: 建物は<tips=82>広美</tips>の記憶とは変わっていたが、その表札にはしっかりと『UCHIDA』という文字があった。
English: The building has changed from what <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> remembers, but the nameplate clearly reads ‘UCHIDA.’

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>はゴクリと喉を鳴らして生唾を飲み込んだ。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> throat works as she swallows nervously.

Japanese: <tips=9>Y地区</tips>の憂鬱な曇り空に慣れた<tips=82>広美</tips>にとって、その青空と太陽の輝きはあまりにも鮮やかに目に沁みた。
English: After growing accustomed to the dreary overcast skies of <tips=9>Y District</tips>, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> found the blue sky and the brilliance of the sun almost painfully vivid.

Japanese: アスファルトの上に濃い影をくっきりと作り出す強い日差しの下、彼女はそろそろと手を持ち上げて、インターフォンのボタンにその指先を触れる。
English: Beneath the fierce sunlight, which cast dense, sharp-edged shadows upon the asphalt, she slowly raised her hand and touched the tip of one finger to the intercom button.

Japanese: プラスチックの艶やかな感触を人差し指に感じる。
English: She felt the sleek plastic against the tip of her index finger.

Japanese: この目の前の、どこにでもある普通の一軒家のなかに、<tips=82>広美</tips>にとってたったひとつの家庭がある。
English: Inside the ordinary detached house before her—one like any other—was the one and only home <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> had.

Japanese: もう何年も、全く別の生活を送ってきた彼らだが、身体に流れる血のつながりと、昔の思い出は共有しており、誰にも拭い去ることは出来ない。
English: They had lived entirely separate lives for years now, but they shared the blood in their veins and the memories of long ago, and no one could wipe those away.

Japanese: 今この指にほんの少しの力を入れるだけで、それぞれの生活を隔てて来た見えない壁が崩れ去り、お互いの生活のなかにお互いが姿を現すのだ。
English: The slightest pressure from this finger would bring down the invisible wall that had divided their lives. Each would appear once more within the life of the other.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は緊張して喉をごくりとならしたが、口の中はからからに乾いて飲み込むものはなかった。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> swallowed nervously, though her mouth was so dry that there was nothing to swallow.

Japanese: 風が吹き、木の葉がざわざわと擦れ合う音が聞こえる。車が通り過ぎるエンジンの音が聞こえる。
English: The wind blew, and she heard leaves rustling against one another. She heard the engine of a passing car.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は指をインターフォンから離し、溜息をついた。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> drew her finger away from the intercom and sighed.

Japanese: さっきまであんなに楽しみにしていたのに、いざとなると勇気が出ない。
English: Only moments ago, she had been looking forward to this so eagerly. Now that the moment has come, she cannot summon the courage.

Japanese: 彼女はまったく、今の家族たちの様子を知らないのだ。少し、どんな風だか見てみようと、敷地を取り囲む生け垣に沿って歩きながら家の様子をうかがった。
English: She knew nothing at all about what her family was like now. Thinking that she would take just a brief look, Hiromi walked along the hedge surrounding the property and peered toward the house.

Japanese: 側面にまわったところで背伸びをして覗き込むと、庭の光景が目に入る。
English: When she reached the side, she stood on tiptoe and looked over it. The garden came into view.

Japanese: 一畳ほどの小さな家庭菜園があって、ミニトマトが実っている。庭の隅にこんもりと小さく盛り上がった上に『クロ』と書かれた板が刺さっているのはペットの墓でもつくったんだろうか。縁側に上がるところには、サンダルが二足ならんでいる。
English: There is a little vegetable patch, no larger than a single tatami mat, where cherry tomatoes grow. In one corner of the garden, a board marked ‘KURO’ sticks out of a small, gently rounded mound. Had they made a grave for a pet? Two pairs of sandals stand side by side at the step up to the veranda.

Japanese: そしてガラスのサッシの向こうには、リビングルームの様子が見えた。
English: Beyond the glass doors, she could see into the living room.

Japanese: はっきりした木目が浮かび上がったキャメルのフローリングに白い壁のシンプルな洋室。大きな液晶テレビ。ニスで艶光りする木製の棚の上には、写真立てが並べられている。壁に掛かった賞状は妹が学校でとったものだろうか。ここからではその文字までは読めない。
English: It was a simple Western-style room, with white walls and camel-colored flooring whose grain stood out clearly. There was a large flat-screen television. Framed photographs lined the top of a varnished wooden cabinet. Had her sister won the certificate hanging on the wall at school? Hiromi could not read the words from here.

Japanese: そして中央に設置された六人掛けのテーブルの上には、サラダの入った大きなボウルと、口のところが銀紙のようなものでパッケージされた飲み物の瓶とグラス、そして白いホールケーキがあった。
English: On the six-seat table in the center of the room sit a large bowl of salad; glasses and a bottle with silver foil around its mouth; and a whole white cake.

Japanese: それを見た時<tips=82>広美</tips>の胸はざわついた。
English: The sight sent a restless stirring through <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> chest.

Japanese: 誰かの誕生日パーティをやろうとしているのだろうか。それは、父親か、母親か、それとも妹か。
English: Were they about to hold a birthday party for someone? Was it her father, her mother, or her sister?

Japanese: 思い出そうとしてみたけれど、今日が何日かわからない。携帯電話で確認してから、それ以前に家族の誕生日を誰一人として知らないことに気がついた。
English: She tried to remember, but she did not know the date. After checking it on her phone, she realized that she did not know the birthday of a single member of her family in the first place.

Japanese: 誰もいなかったその部屋に、奥のキッチンから一人の人物が現れた。
English: A person emerged from the kitchen at the back of the empty room.

Japanese: それは紛れもない母の姿だった。髪型を変え、少し老けて印象が変わっていたが一目でそうとわかった。
English: It was unmistakably her mother. She had changed her hairstyle and aged a little, altering her appearance, but Hiromi knew her at a glance.

Japanese: 母は両手にお盆を持ち、その上に今日の料理を盛った皿を乗せていた。
English: Her mother carried a tray in both hands, with plates laden with food for the occasion arranged upon it.

Japanese: 予期していたはずなのに、それはあまりにも突然の邂逅に感じられた。<tips=82>広美</tips>は心臓が止まりそうな思いをしながらとっさに姿を生け垣に隠し、その葉の隙間からなかの様子をこっそりと覗く。
English: Although <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> should have expected it, the encounter felt overwhelmingly sudden. Her heart nearly stopped. She ducked behind the hedge on instinct and secretly watched the room through the gaps between its leaves.

Japanese: 母はこちらに気づくことなく、皿をテーブルの上に並べている。
English: Her mother noticed nothing and began arranging the plates upon the table.

Japanese: そしてすぐにもう一人の人物が別のドアを開けて部屋のなかに入って来た。
English: Then, almost immediately, another person opened a different door and entered the room.

Japanese: 少し腹が突き出て、頭髪が寂しくなっているがそれは間違いなく父だ。
English: His belly protruded a little and his hair had thinned, but he was unmistakably her father.

Japanese: 父は両手にリボンでラッピングされた箱を持っており、母に見せると二人で笑い合う。
English: Her father held a ribbon-wrapped box in both hands. When he showed it to her mother, the two of them laughed together.

Japanese: 言葉を交わしたのちに、箱をテレビの裏に隠した。
English: After exchanging a few words, he hid the box behind the television.

Japanese: あれで、今日の主役を驚かせようと言うのだ。
English: They meant to use it to surprise the guest of honor today.

Japanese: そう、今日は妹の誕生日で、家族はそれを盛りあげるための準備をしているに違いない。
English: Yes—today must be her sister’s birthday, and the family must be preparing to celebrate.

Japanese: 父は落ち着かない様子のままソファーに座り、新聞を手に取ったり戻したりしていた。
English: Her father sat restlessly on the sofa, picking up the newspaper only to put it down again.

Japanese: その足元にはいつのまにか部屋に入っていた小さな毛むくじゃらの犬がじゃれつき、父はそれを抱き上げる。
English: A little shaggy dog that had slipped into the room at some point frisked around his feet, and he lifted it into his arms.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は凍り付いたようにそのガラスを隔てた絵に描いたような平和な光景に見入っていた。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> stood frozen, staring through the glass at a scene of perfect peace, as though it had been painted there.

Japanese: それは、<tips=82>広美</tips>が発症する前にこの家にあった光景だ。そして、<tips=82>広美</tips>が発症してからはこのように完全にくつろいだ光景はなかった。本来ならここに自分も居たのだろうか？　いや、あのまま自分がここにいたら、彼らはこのように笑う日は来なかったかもしれない。自分がいなくなることで、彼らはこの幸福を作れたのだろう。でも、今の自分なら？
English: It was the kind of scene this house had held before <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> onset. After <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> onset, there had never again been such a scene of complete ease. By rights, would she have been there among them? No. If she had stayed, perhaps the day would never have come when they could smile this way. Perhaps they had built this happiness because she was gone. But what if it were her as she was now?

Japanese: 胸がどきどきとして、おかしな汗がこめかみを伝う。
English: Her heart pounds, and an unfamiliar trickle of sweat runs down her temple.

Japanese: 母はケーキの上に小さな蝋燭を並べ、父がそれにライターで火をつける。全ての着火が終わると、部屋の電気は消され、カーテンが閉められた。そして、妹を呼ぶ父の声が聞こえる。
English: Her mother arranged small candles upon the cake, and her father lit them with a lighter. Once every flame was burning, they switched off the lights and closed the curtains. Then she heard her father call for her sister.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は閉め出されたような格好でしばらくそこに立っていたが、すぐに移動して部屋のなかを見られる場所を探す。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> stood there for a moment as though she had been shut out. Then she moved at once, searching for somewhere else from which she could see into the room.

Japanese: 別の壁に小さな窓があり、生け垣の土台となっているブロックの上に上れば、なんとかそこからテーブルの近くを見ることが出来た。
English: There was a small window in another wall. By climbing onto the blocks forming the hedge’s foundation, she could just manage to see the area around the table.

Japanese: そして、ちょうど自分の席に座ろうとしている妹の姿が見えた。
English: There she saw her sister, just as the girl was about to take her seat.

Japanese: 彼女は、一目でそうとわかった両親とは違い、記憶のなかよりもずっと成長して、まるで別人のようだった。街で偶然見かけてもその顔立ちだけでは気がつかないかもしれない。でも、もしかしたら、と振り返りはするだろう。
English: Unlike her parents, whom Hiromi recognized at once, her sister has grown so far beyond the child in her memory that she seems almost another person. If they happened to pass on the street, Hiromi might not recognize her from her face alone. Even so, something might make her turn for a second look.

Japanese: なぜなら、幸せそうに目を輝かせる彼女の顔の半分には、この幸福そのものの光景にはあまりにも不似合いなみにくい火傷のあとがあったからだ。
English: For half of that happy face, its eyes alight, bore an ugly burn scar terribly out of place in this picture of happiness.

Japanese: 「あっ」
English: “Ah—”

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>の身体ががくがくと震え、その拍子に足をすべらせてブロック塀から落ちてアスファルトに尻餅をつく。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> body begins to shake violently. In the trembling she loses her footing on the blocks and lands hard on her backside on the asphalt.

Japanese: そして立ち上がると、駆け出した。どこへ行こうというつもりもなく、とにかくこの場を離れたかった。その顔は蒼白で、引きつっていた。
English: Then she rose and ran. She had no destination in mind; she simply had to get away. Her face was bloodless and drawn tight.

Japanese: インターフォンなど押せるわけがない。自分が、あの幸せな誕生日パーティを邪魔出来るだろうか？　あのささやかな幸せを取り戻した家庭に戻れるだろうか？　あの妹の顔に消えない痣を作ったのは自分なのだ。
English: She could never press that intercom. How could she intrude upon that happy birthday party? How could she return to a family that had recovered this modest happiness? She was the one who had left that permanent scar upon her sister’s face.

Japanese: （どうして忘れていたんだろう？　どうしてなの？　戻れるわけなんかないじゃないか！）
English: (How could I have forgotten? How? Of course I can never go back!)

Japanese: 走る<tips=82>広美</tips>の目に涙が浮かんで丸いたまとなり、それが崩れるようにボロボロと頬の上を流れ落ちた。
English: Tears swelled into round drops as <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> ran, then broke loose and streamed down her cheeks.

Japanese: 家で暮らしていた最後の日々、<tips=82>広美</tips>は完全に別の世界の住人となっていた。
English: During her final days at home, <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> had become a resident of another world entirely.

Japanese: 一緒に住む二人の大人と一人の幼児は、見た目は家族にそっくりだが、その正体はまったく別の恐ろしいものだ。きっと宇宙人に違いない。いつのまにか入れ替わって、自分をいつも見張っている。そして大事なものを奪おうとしているんだ。
English: The two adults and the small child who lived with her looked exactly like her family, but beneath those appearances they were something else—something terrible. They had to be aliens. At some point they had replaced her real family and begun watching her constantly. They meant to take away everything precious to her.

Japanese: 宇宙人は火に弱いと、別の声が教えてくれる。その声はいつも優しくて、<tips=82>広美</tips>を肯定してくれる天使の声だから信用出来る。火を使って、宇宙人を追い出せば優しい両親と、かわいい妹が帰ってきてくれるんだ。早くあの懐かしい家族に会いたい！
English: Another voice tells her that aliens are weak against fire. The voice is always gentle, always affirms <tips=82>Hiromi</tips>, and is the voice of an angel, so she can trust it. If she uses fire to drive out the aliens, her kind parents and adorable little sister will come back. She wants to see that beloved family again as soon as she can!

Japanese: 夜にこっそり起き出すと雑誌をちぎって紙切れをうずたかく山にした。<tips=82>広美</tips>の症状が出るようになってからライターはみな鍵付きの戸棚に仕舞われていたが、この日のために来客がハンガーにかけたジャケットからひとつ抜き取ってある。それを使って、紙くずに火をつけた。さっき父親が蝋燭に火をつけたように。メラメラと炎があがり、臭い煙が立ち上って部屋に充満する。火災警報器がけたたましい音を立てる。恍惚の表情で炎を眺めていた<tips=82>広美</tips>はその音でビクッと肩をふるわし、部屋を飛び出る。
English: At night she had slipped out of bed, torn magazines to pieces, and heaped the scraps high. Since <tips=82>Hiromi’s</tips> symptoms first appeared, every lighter in the house had been locked in a cabinet, but in preparation for this day she had taken one from a visitor’s jacket left on a hanger. She used it to set the paper scraps alight, just as her father had lit the candles moments earlier. Flames leapt up, and foul-smelling smoke rose and filled the room. The fire alarm shrieked. <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> had been gazing at the flames in rapture, but the sound made her shoulders jerk and sent her bolting from the room.

Japanese: 「あの音を止めて！　宇宙語で私の悪口を言っているの！」
English: “Make that noise stop! It’s saying terrible things about me in alien language!”

Japanese: 一度も思い出したことがないその光景が、ありありと<tips=82>広美</tips>の脳裏に蘇った。その夜すこし肌寒かったことや、隣の犬が狂ったように吠えていたことも思い出した。
English: The scene, which had never returned to her before, came back to <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> with perfect clarity. She even remembered that the night had been slightly cold and that the neighbor’s dog had barked like mad.

Japanese: そうだ自分は散々迷惑をかけて、その挙げ句に焼き殺そうとしたんだ。結果妹は顔に消えない痣を作った。女の子が顔にあんな痣を作って、どれだけつらい人生を送ってきたのだろうか。全て自分がやったんだ。
English: Yes. She had caused them endless misery and then, at the end of it all, tried to burn them to death. Her sister had been left with a permanent scar across her face. What kind of painful life must a girl have endured with a scar like that? Hiromi had done all of it.

Japanese: たとえ病気のせいとは言え、言い訳出来るようなものではない。もう症状が消えましたと、何食わぬ顔で家に戻ることなんか出来るはずもない。
English: Even if her illness had caused it, that was no excuse. She could not simply go home as though nothing had happened and announce that her symptoms were gone.

Japanese: あの頃みたいに、妹は怯えて引きつった顔でこちらを見、両親は何かあるたびまた無茶苦茶なことをするのではないかとビクビクと怯えて暮らすことになるのだろう。
English: Her sister would look at her with the same frightened, rigid expression as before. Her parents would spend their lives cowering, afraid that every small event might drive her to do something senseless again.

Japanese: そもそも本当に症状が消えたのか？　こんな大事なことを忘れて、すっかり元通りになれると信じていただなんて、どう考えたって普通じゃない。
English: Were her symptoms truly gone in the first place? She had forgotten something this important, yet believed completely that she could simply return to how she had been. No matter how she considered it, that was not normal.

Japanese: <tips=82>広美</tips>は泣きながら、やみくもに走った。
English: <tips=82>Hiromi</tips> ran blindly, weeping.

Japanese: それから先自分がどこをどう行動したのか覚えていない。
English: She remembered nothing of where she went or what she did afterward.

Japanese: ただ気がつけば雨でびしょ濡れになって、<tips=9>Y地区</tips>に居た。うなだれ、どこともわからない通りを歩いている。酔っ払った客が時々何か下品な言葉をかけてくるが、世界の果てで囁いているようで耳に入ってこない。いまの<tips=82>広美</tips>にとって、周囲で起きている全てのことが地球の裏側の出来事のように遠かった。
English: When she next became aware of her surroundings, she was drenched by rain and back in <tips=9>Y District</tips>. Her head bowed, she walked down a street she did not recognize. Drunken customers occasionally called something vulgar to her, but their words seemed to be whispered at the end of the world and never reached her ears. Now, to <tips=82>Hiromi</tips>, everything happening around her felt as remote as events on the other side of the earth.

Japanese: 動揺はしていない。気持ちはもう大分落ち着いていた。
English: She was no longer distraught. Her emotions had already settled considerably.

Japanese: 結局、自分のことばかり考えていたんだ。相手のことを考えたり、想像したりすることが出来なかった。だから実際相手の暮らしを見るまで何も気づかなかった。
English: In the end, she had thought only of herself. She had been unable to consider the other people involved, or even imagine their lives. Not until she saw those lives for herself had she understood anything.

Japanese: 彼らの暮らしは自分とは余りに違った。病院でわがままに暮らし、そして世話してくれた人たちの血みどろの亡骸をそれほどの感情もなく踏み越え、今度は家族と元通り幸せに暮らそうだなんて、そんな都合のいいことがどうして思えよう？

Japanese: 近くに<tips=15>ボーダーエリア</tips>の住民らしい、頭からすっぽりとかぶって全身を隠す服を着た人物が畑の草むしりをしているのに気がつく。
English: Nearby, I noticed someone weeding a field, wrapped from head to toe in the concealing clothing worn by residents of the <tips=15>Border Area</tips>.

Japanese: 「すまないが、ここを二人組が通らなかったか教えてくれないか？」
English: “Excuse me. Could you tell me whether a pair of people passed this way?”

Japanese: 「ふたりぐみ？」
English: “A pair?”

Japanese: 顔を上げてそう言った声は、服装では性別の区別がつかなかったが、若い女のものだった。
English: The clothes concealed the person’s sex, but the voice that answered when they raised their head belonged to a young woman.

Japanese: 「若い女の子と、白人の老人なんだが……」
English: “A young girl and an elderly white man…”

Japanese: 画像を見せるのももどかしく、返答を急かした。
English: Too impatient even to show her the image, I pressed her for an answer.

Japanese: 彼女は頷くと、奥の方を指さした。
English: She nodded and pointed farther in.

Japanese: 「いまさっき、そちらへ。あんまり奥に行くと汚染されてますよって教えてあげたんですけれど、大丈夫ですって女の子がこたえて……」
English: “They went that way just a moment ago. I told them it was contaminated farther in, but the girl said they would be all right...”

Japanese: 「いまさっきって、具体的にどれくらい？」
English: “How long is ‘just a moment’ exactly?”

Japanese: 「はっきりわからないですけど、五分くらいかな……」
English: “I’m not certain. Perhaps five minutes...”

Japanese: 「ありがとう」
English: “Thank you.”

Japanese: やっと、追いついたぞ。
English: At last. I had caught up.

Japanese: <tips=8>グレートホール</tips>に向かうその道は使うものがすくなく、廃墟の間に低い雑草がまばらに生い茂っている。入ってすぐに立ち入り禁止のロープがあったが、杭の金具が錆びて地面に落ちていた。この先を少し行くと一応汚染区域ということになっているが、子どもなどはよく遊び場にしているし、ゴミの不法投棄なども行われている。
English: Few people used the path toward the <tips=8>Great Hole</tips>, and sparse, low weeds grew between the ruins. A no-entry rope hung just inside, but the metal fitting on its post had rusted through and fallen to the ground. The area a short distance ahead was officially contaminated, yet children often used it as a playground, and people dumped refuse there illegally.

Japanese: 私はそのロープを踏み越え、辺りに人影がないのを確認してから、銃を取り出した。
English: I stepped over the rope, confirmed that no one else was in sight, and drew the pistol.

Japanese: ギロギロと辺りを睨むようにして二人の姿を探しながら、道を進む。
English: I stalked down the path, glaring this way and that as I searched for the pair.

Japanese: 謝罪も言い訳も必要ない。相手にこれから死ぬ理由を教える気もない。だから言葉を交わすつもりはない。見つけたら、すぐにその背中を撃つ。幸い風は前から吹いている。相手の感覚も私と同じように研ぎ澄まされているかもしれないが、この条件なら先に私が見つけるだろう。見つければ、あとはなんとかして拳銃の射程まで近づき、<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>を撃つ。
English: There would be no apologies or excuses. I had no intention of telling him why he was about to die. I had no intention of speaking at all. Once I found him, I would immediately shoot him in the back. Fortunately, the wind blew toward me. His senses might be sharpened like mine, but under these conditions, I should see him first. Then I merely had to get within handgun range somehow and shoot <tips=20>Koschei</tips>.

Japanese: 灰上の方は無視をする。狙いは<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>ただ一人。
English: I would ignore Haigami. <tips=20>Koschei</tips> alone was my target.

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>は私と同様不死身の身体を持っているが、その効力を失わせる方法は知っている。死んだ<tips=55>汐松子</tips>の身体に、犯人から『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』を注射されたと思われる形跡があった。警察はなぜこんなものが被害者に注射されたのかわからないようだったが、私にはその理由がわかる。
English: <tips=20>Koschei</tips> possessed an immortal body like mine, but I knew how to take that power away. Marks on <tips=55>Matsuko Shio’s</tips> body suggested that her killer had injected her with <tips=46>Neo Rose</tips>. The police did not understand why a victim would be given such a drug. I knew the reason.

Japanese: 警察は知らなかったが、<tips=55>汐松子</tips>は不死身の身体を持っている。彼女が殺されるというのは本来ありえないことだ。不死身の身体に詳しい<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>が、なぜ<tips=55>汐松子</tips>にわざわざ『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』を使ったのか。つまりそれが不死の能力を消す方法なのだろう。
English: The police had not known that <tips=55>Matsuko Shio</tips> possessed an immortal body. Ordinarily, killing her should have been impossible. Why had <tips=20>Koschei</tips>, who understood immortality intimately, gone out of his way to use ‘<tips=46>Neo Rose</tips>’ on <tips=55>Matsuko Shio</tips>? The drug was presumably the means of eliminating immortality.

Japanese: 私の銃には『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』が弾頭に仕込まれた特製の弾丸が装填されている。そして、『<tips=46>ネオ・ローズ</tips>』の注射も用意している。
English: My pistol was loaded with custom rounds whose tips had been packed with ‘<tips=46>Neo Rose</tips>.’ I had also prepared an injection of ‘<tips=46>Neo Rose</tips>.’

Japanese: 無論、相手の能力を考えれば銃だけで仕留めなくてはならないが、もし弾丸を撃ち尽くしてしまった場合は、こんなものでも持っていた方がマシだろう。
English: Of course, given my opponent’s abilities, I would have to finish him with the gun alone. But if I used up every bullet, even something like this would be better than nothing.

Japanese: とにかく、あとちょっとだ！
English: In any event, only a little farther!

Japanese: 気持ちがはやり、駆け出したくなるが、物音はなるべく抑えなくてはいけない。私は銃を両手で構えたまま競歩選手のように早足で道を進む。
English: Impatience drove me onward and made me want to break into a run, but I had to keep my movements as quiet as possible. Holding the gun in both hands, I hurried down the path with the short, rapid steps of a racewalker.

Japanese: もし二人が道を逸れて廃墟の中へ入ってしまっていたら見つけられない。また、さっきの<tips=15>ボーダーエリア</tips>の女の情報が人違いだったら、やっぱり遭遇は難しいだろう。
English: If the two of them had left the path and entered the ruins, I would never find them. And if the information from the woman in the <tips=15>Border Area</tips> concerned the wrong people, I was unlikely to encounter them either.

Japanese: 確実というわけじゃない。それでも、今はこの道を進むしかない。他に選択肢はないのだ。
English: Nothing was certain. Even so, all I could do now was follow this road. There was no other choice.

Japanese: ――そして、その瞬間は不意に訪れた。
English: —And then, without warning, the moment came.

Japanese: 幸運に、思わず声が出そうになる。
English: I nearly cried out at my good fortune.

Japanese: 道の向こうに二人が歩いている後ろ姿を発見したのだ。声は聞こえないが、彼らは何か喋っているらしく、時折顔を向かい合わせている。
English: Ahead on the road, I caught sight of the two of them walking with their backs to me. I could not hear their voices, but they seemed to be talking, occasionally turning to look at one another.

Japanese: その歩みは遅い。
English: They walked slowly.

Japanese: そして、まだこちらには気がついていない。
English: And they had not yet noticed me.

Japanese: このまままっすぐ道を行くか、脇の茂みに隠れて回り込むようにして近づくか、選択を迫られた。
English: I had to choose between continuing straight down the path and hiding in the undergrowth to circle closer.

Japanese: 茂みに隠れれば、姿を隠すことが出来るが音が出る。このまま背後から近づけば、音はさほどではないが、何かの拍子でどちらかが振り返ったら身を隠す方法がない。
English: The undergrowth would conceal me, but it would make noise. If I kept approaching directly from behind, I would make far less noise—but if either of them happened to look back, I would have nowhere to hide.

Japanese: 私はまっすぐ進むことを選んだ。大した計算があったわけじゃない。目の前のターゲットに近づくための最短距離を反射的に選んでいたというだけのことだ。
English: I chose to continue straight ahead. There was no elaborate calculation behind it. I had simply taken, by reflex, the shortest route to the target in front of me. That was all.

Japanese: 銃自体の有効射程は八十メートルほどあるらしいが、私の技術ではその距離で命中させるのは難しい。<tips=17>タイプＢ</tips>能力によって以前よりそうした動作は精密になっているはずだが、それでも五十から六十メートルでやっと人型のどこかを捉えられるといったところだ。ある程度の確実性を得るためには、最低四十メートルの距離までは近づきたい。
English: The gun itself apparently had an effective range of about eighty meters, but with my skill it would be difficult to hit anything at that distance. My <tips=17>Type B</tips> abilities should have made such movements more precise than before, yet even at fifty or sixty meters, I could only hope to hit some part of a human silhouette. To have any reasonable degree of certainty, I wanted to get within forty meters.

Japanese: 私は相手のどちらも振り返らぬよう祈りつつ、早足で背中を追う。
English: Praying neither of them would turn around, I hurried after their retreating backs.

Japanese: 二人は話に夢中になっているのか、私の存在に気がつかない。近づくにつれて風に乗って小さくその話し声が聞こえてきたが、その内容まではわからない。
English: Perhaps they were absorbed in conversation, because neither noticed me. As I drew closer, their quiet voices came to me on the wind, but I still could not make out what they were saying.

Japanese: とにかく、私は彼らを射程におさめることが出来た。
English: At last, I had them within range.

Japanese: 私は銃を持ち上げ、照準を灰上の隣にいる小柄な老人にあわせた。あれは<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>が変身したものだとは思うが、見たことのない姿だ。可能性としては人違いということもありうる。
English: I raised the gun and trained the sights on the small old man beside Haigami. I assumed he was <tips=20>Koschei</tips> transformed, but I had never seen this guise before. It was still possible I had the wrong man.

Japanese: しかし、悠長に確認していれば、せっかくのチャンスを逃してしまう。
English: But if I took the time to make certain, I would lose this chance.

Japanese: まあいい。人違いなら、そのときはそのときだ。
English: Fine. If I had the wrong man, so be it.

Japanese: 呼吸を整え、静かに引き金にかけた指に力を入れる。
English: I steadied my breathing and slowly tightened my finger on the trigger.

Japanese: まさに弾が発射されようとする瞬間——。
English: At the very instant the bullet was about to leave the barrel—

Japanese: 「やめて」
English: “Don’t.”

Japanese: と、すぐ耳元で声が囁いた。
English: A voice whispered right beside my ear.

Japanese: それは<tips=53>ミユキ</tips>の声だ。
English: It was <tips=53>Miyuki’s</tips> voice.

Japanese: ああ、こんなときに発作が！
English: Of all the times for an episode!

Japanese: しかし、私はこれが幻聴なのはわかっている。乱れた呼吸をすぐに整え直す。
English: But I knew it was a hallucination. I quickly forced my ragged breathing back under control.

Japanese: この僅かな時間の遅れが運命を分けた。
English: That tiny delay made all the difference.

Japanese: 先ほどまでそんなそぶりも見せなかった灰上が、不意にこちらを振り向いたのである。
English: Haigami, who until then had shown no sign that she knew I was there, suddenly turned to look at me.

Japanese: まずい！
English: Damn!

Japanese: 私はすぐに引き金を引いたが、遅かった。両腕に見えない力が加わる。
English: I pulled the trigger at once, but I was too late. An invisible force bore down on both my arms.

Japanese: 銃口が火を吹き、爆音がしたものの、照準は完全に逸れていて、目標は微動だにしない。
English: The gun roared and spat flame, but my aim had been thrown completely off, and my target did not so much as flinch.

Japanese: 再度狙いをつけようとするが、見えない力は強力で、私は照準をあわせることが出来ない。
English: I tried to take aim again, but the invisible force was too powerful; I could not line up the sights.

Japanese: ぶれたまま引き金を引いてみたが、彼らの足元の土が跳ねただけで、とても命中には至らない。
English: I tried pulling the trigger while my aim still wavered, but all it did was kick up dirt at their feet. The shot came nowhere close to hitting them.

Japanese: 今の人間離れをしているはずの私の腕力でも、対抗することが出来ないとは。
English: Even my strength, which should now have been beyond human, was no match for it.

Japanese: おそらくこれが、警官の首をねじって殺した力の正体なのだ。
English: This was probably the true nature of the force that had twisted the police officers’ necks and killed them.

Japanese: 「くそっ！」
English: “Damn it!”

Japanese: 叫ぶ私を、少女がらんらんと光る金色の目で見つめている。
English: As I shouted, the girl stared at me, her golden eyes blazing.

Japanese: やはりやつも、ハイブリッドなのか。
English: Was she a hybrid too, after all?

Japanese: 奇襲に失敗した以上、逃走を図るべきなのはわかっていたが、私は前に駆け出した。ここまで来て逃げられるものか。
English: Now that my surprise attack had failed, I knew I should run, but instead I charged forward. I had come too far to flee now.

Japanese: 無理矢理近づけば、ぶれる銃口でも標的を捉えることが出来る。
English: If I forced my way closer, even a wavering muzzle could find its target.

Japanese: 「来ないで……」
English: “Don’t come any closer...”

Japanese: 灰上の言葉と共に、見えない力が私を押し返す。それに対抗するためにぐっと足腰に力を入れると、足元の土がえぐれた。
English: At Haigami's words, an invisible force pushed me back. I planted my feet and braced my entire lower body against it, gouging the earth beneath me.

Japanese: かまうものか。
English: As if I cared.

Japanese: 全身の力を込めて、もう一歩踏み込む。
English: Putting the strength of my whole body behind it, I forced myself one more step forward.

Japanese: 「うおおおおっ」
English: “Raaaaah!”

Japanese: 僅かに私の力が上回るようだ。私の身体はじりじりと前に進む。
English: My strength seemed to hold a slight advantage. Inch by inch, I advanced.

Japanese: その時には、灰上の隣の老人も振り返っている。
English: By then, the old man beside Haigami had turned around as well.

Japanese: それは<tips=65>ヘス</tips>でもない、やはり私の知らない人物だ。
English: He was not <tips=65>Hess</tips>. As I had thought, he was someone I did not recognize.

Japanese: しかし、あれが<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>なのだ。
English: Yet this was <tips=20>Koschei</tips>.

Japanese: もしあれが、あのテレポート少女にでも変身して襲ってくれば絶体絶命だ。
English: If he transformed into the teleporting girl and attacked, I would be finished.

Japanese: そうでなくとも、あの<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>本体にも何か特別な力があるかもしれない。灰上の見えない力と全力で押し相撲をしている私は、何をされても簡単に殺されるだろう。勝算はほとんどない。
English: Even if that was not the case, <tips=20>Koschei</tips> himself might possess some special power of his own. Locked in a full-strength shoving match with Haigami’s invisible force, I would be easy prey for anything he might do. I had almost no chance of winning.

Japanese: やはり、相手に気づかれた時点で逃げるしかなかったのだ。今からでもくるりと後ろを向いて走り出すべきなのだ。
English: I should have fled the moment they noticed me, after all. Even now, I should turn around and run.

Japanese: それは理解していたが、激情が理性的な行動を私に許さなかった。
English: I understood that, but my rage would not permit me to act rationally.

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>は変身しなかった。かといって逃げようとするわけでもない。
English: <tips=20>Koschei</tips> did not transform. Nor did he try to flee.

Japanese: 私に向かって一歩、近づいた。
English: He took one step toward me.

Japanese: 「<tips=63>サーシェンカ</tips>！」
English: “<tips=63>Sashenka</tips>!”

Japanese: 灰上が声をあげる。
English: Haigami cried out.

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>はその声が聞こえないかのように、ただ私を見つめ、そして近づいてくる。
English: <tips=20>Koschei</tips> merely stared at me as though he could not hear her and kept coming closer.

Japanese: その時私は歯を食いしばって、前に進もうとしていた。
English: At that moment, I was gritting my teeth and struggling to move forward.

Japanese: 体中の肌が充血で真っ赤に染まり、頭の角もあいまって、文字通り鬼のような形相になっていただろう。
English: The skin all over my body was flushed bright red, and with the horns on my head, I must literally have looked like an ogre.

Japanese: 「アナタは……」
English: “You ARE...”

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>はそう呼びかけた。
English: <tips=20>Koschei</tips> addressed me.

Japanese: 私はなんとか両手を持ち上げて銃を構え、彼に狙いを定める。
English: Somehow I raised both hands and leveled the gun, taking aim at him.

Japanese: 大分距離が縮まっており、この距離ならある程度ぶれても外れないはずだ。
English: The distance between us had narrowed considerably. From this close, even if my aim wavered somewhat, I should not miss.

Japanese: しかし、顔面に狙いをつけた瞬間、それまで私の全身にかかっていた圧力が、全て両手へと移動した。
English: But the instant I aimed at his face, all the pressure that had been bearing down on my whole body shifted to my hands.

Japanese: その結果、照準は大きく上にずれて私は白い雲を撃つ。
English: As a result, my aim jerked high, and I fired into the white clouds.

Japanese: 「貴様っ！　くそっ！」
English: “You bastard! Damn you!”

Japanese: 灰上の圧力と戦う私を、<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>は静かな目でじっと見つめている。
English: As I fought against Haigami's pressure, <tips=20>Koschei</tips> watched me with calm, unwavering eyes.

Japanese: 「探偵さんっ！」
English: “Detective!”

Japanese: 灰上が声をあげる。
English: Haigami cried out.

Japanese: 「もう帰って！　今私はあなたを殺そうと思えば簡単に殺せるんだよっ！」
English: “Go home! I could kill you easily right now if I wanted to!”

Japanese: 私はその声を無視して、もう一度銃を構えようとするが、どうやっても銃口は暴れてしまって<tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>をとらえることが出来ない。
English: I ignored her and tried once more to level the gun, but no matter what I did, the muzzle bucked wildly and I could not get <tips=20>Koschei</tips> in my sights.

Japanese: 「ああ、そうか。アナタは、やっぱりあの時の……」
English: “Ah, I see. You really are the one from back then...”

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>はそう呟く。
English: <tips=20>Koschei</tips> murmured the words.

Japanese: 「ぼくがあなたの大事な人を奪ってしまったんデスね……」
English: “I took someone precious from you, DIDN’T I...?”

Japanese: 彼はそう言って、しわだらけの目を細めた。
English: He narrowed his wrinkled eyes.

Japanese: その表情は悲しそうに見える。これは、どういう人格なのだろう？
English: His expression looked sorrowful. What sort of personality was this?

Japanese: どう見ても演技には見えない。もしかしたら、この人格は殺人にはまったく関わっていないのかもしれない。
English: It did not look like an act at all. Perhaps this personality had had nothing whatsoever to do with any murder.

Japanese: しかし、それは私には関係のないことだ。身体に力を込める。
English: But none of that mattered to me. I tensed every muscle in my body.

Japanese: 向こうで灰上が顔をしかめた。彼女ほど強力な能力者がこれくらいで疲労するとは思えないが、体力が落ちているのかもしれない。
English: Haigami grimaced in the distance. I could hardly believe a psychic as powerful as she was would tire from this alone, but perhaps her stamina had declined.

Japanese: 「取り返しがつかないことをしました。ゴメンなさい」
English: “I did something that can never be undone. I’m SORRY.”

Japanese: <tips=20>コシチェイ</tips>はそう言って、目に涙を浮かべる。
English: Tears gathered in <tips=20>Koschei’s</tips> eyes as he spoke.

Japanese: 謝ったところで、許すつもりなどない。
English: He could apologize all he liked. I had no intention of forgiving him.

Japanese: むしろその態度が私の感情を逆なでする。
English: If anything, his attitude only inflamed me further.

Japanese: 全身にさらなる力を込めるために歯を噛みしめると、奥歯が砕け、口の中に血液があふれた。
English: I clenched my teeth to summon still more strength. One of my molars shattered, and blood flooded my mouth.

Japanese: 血管が切れそうだ。筋肉がちぎれそうだ。だが、私の力がやや上回っている。
English: My blood vessels felt ready to burst. My muscles felt ready to tear. But my strength had a slight edge.

Japanese: 彼女は手加減しているのだろうか？　それとも、やはり弱っているのか？
English: Was she holding back? Or was she weakened after all?

Japanese: 何でも良い。
English: It did not matter which.

Japanese: とにかく、なんとか照準を合わせることが出来そうだ——と、思った瞬間、また力の向きが変わって、私のからだ全体が下から上へと持ち上げられた。
English: In any case, I was just thinking I might finally be able to line up the sights—when the direction of the force changed again, lifting my whole body from below.

Japanese: 前や横からの力なら大地に踏ん張ることが出来るが、上空へと飛ばされてはそれも出来ない。
English: I could brace against force from the front or side by planting myself against the earth, but not if I was hurled into the air.

Japanese: 身体がふわっと持ち上げられる瞬間、咄嗟に地面に手を伸ばして草を掴んだが、もちろんそれで繋ぎ止められるはずもなく、ブチブチと千切れる。
English: As my body drifted upward, I instinctively reached for the ground and grabbed the grass. Naturally it could not hold me; the blades ripped apart with a series of snaps.

Japanese: そして私のからだは空中に舞うこととなった。
