Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>と<tips=14>深沢</tips>の厳重な警戒網を突破するのは非常に困難であったはずだが、この四人の中には初代<tips=47>解放軍</tips>リーダー<tips=10>見土道夫</tips>の盟友にして<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の旧友である<tips=66>田中紺太</tips>も含まれており、何らかの取引があったと見られているがその詳細はあきらかにされていない。
English: Breaking through the strict security cordon maintained by <tips=7>YS</tips> and <tips=14>Fukazawa</tips> should have been exceedingly difficult. But the four included <tips=66>Konta Tanaka</tips>, close ally of the first <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> leader, <tips=10>Michio Mido</tips>, and an old friend of <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips>. It is believed that some form of transaction occurred, though its details have never been disclosed.

Japanese: とまれ、<tips=47>解放軍</tips>の消滅、そして<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の吸収により<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>のこの街における支配力はかつてないほどに高まることになる。
English: At any rate, with the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> eliminated and the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> absorbed, <tips=7>YS's</tips> control over the city would reach unprecedented heights.

Japanese: 地区内の細かい組織を吸収、あるいは壊滅させ、絶対的な存在となった<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>は<tips=9>Y地区</tips>外の組織や警察との緊張をはらみながらも、それから十年間、<tips=81>龍頭</tips><tips=1>謝亮</tips>が兇弾に斃れるまで街を支配し続けるのだった。
English: <tips=7>YS</tips> absorbed or destroyed the district’s smaller organizations and became its absolute power. Despite continuing tension with organizations and police outside <tips=9>Y District</tips>, it ruled the city for the next ten years, until <tips=81>Longtou</tips> <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> fell to an assassin’s bullet.

Japanese: <tips=9>Y地区</tips>のメインストリートである<tips=57>滑走路通り</tips>を歩くと、シャッターを下ろしている店が目に付く。
English: Walking along <tips=9>Y District’s</tips> main thoroughfare, <tips=57>Runway Street</tips>, I notice a conspicuous number of shuttered storefronts.

Japanese: 以前は時間を問わず人であふれていたこの繁華街は、今は見る影もなく閑散としている。目つきの悪い男が酒のにおいをぷんぷんさせて歩き、向こうでは壁を背にボロをまとった子供がうずくまっている。
English: Once crowded at all hours, this entertainment district is now a desolate shadow of its former self. A hard-eyed man walks by reeking of alcohol, while farther on, a child in rags crouches with their back against a wall.

Japanese: 筆者は三年前にもこの街を訪れている。
English: The author also visited this city three years ago.

Japanese: その時は今よりもずっと栄えてはいたが、しかしそれでも、最盛期と比べるとすっかり寂しくなってしまったと感じさせられた。
English: At the time, the city was far more prosperous than it is now; even so, compared with its heyday, it already felt utterly forlorn.

Japanese: この通りがもっとも賑やかだったのは十年ほど前、高名な<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>の最晩年の時期になるのだろう。
English: This street was probably at its liveliest around ten years ago, during the final years of the renowned <tips=3>Chris Tse</tips>.

Japanese: 当時は<tips=9>Y地区</tips>と言えば日本で最も猥雑で、危険で、雑多なもののあふれた地域であり、訪れる客の他にも、目をギラギラとさせたストリートチルドレンや、あてもなくふらつく未治療の<tips=17>タイプB</tips>発症者の姿があちこちに見られたが、三年前のその頃にはほとんど見られなくなっていた。
English: Back then, <tips=9>Y District</tips> was the most sordid, dangerous, and chaotically diverse neighborhood in Japan. Alongside the visitors, one saw street children with hungry, glittering eyes and untreated sufferers of <tips=17>Type B</tips> wandering aimlessly everywhere. By three years ago, however, they had all but vanished.

Japanese: 街並みは清潔に整えられ、ハンバーガーショップやコンビニエンスストアが進出し、かつて路上に響き渡る大きな売り声を上げていた異形の<tips=16>タイプA</tips>たちは、チェーン店の制服で<tips=77>特質変異</tips>を隠してノーマルの作る社会に溶け込んでいた。
English: The streets had been cleaned up and put in order, hamburger restaurants and convenience stores had moved in, and the misshapen <tips=16>Type As</tips> whose loud hawking cries once rang through the streets now hid their <tips=77>trait mutations</tips> beneath chain-store uniforms and blended into the society built by Normals.

Japanese: 治安は向上し、置き引きや<ruby=すり>掏摸</ruby>に出会うこともなかった。誰でも安心してその繁栄を享受できる、豊かな街になっていた。そして、かつてそこにあった猥雑さや混沌は完全に影を潜めてしまった。
English: Public safety had improved. I encountered neither thieves preying on unattended belongings nor pickpockets. It had become a prosperous city whose abundance anyone could enjoy without fear. And the seediness and chaos that had once existed there had disappeared completely.

Japanese: それはこの街らしさを失ったということでもある反面、平和と秩序がもたらされたということであり、長い間、様々な理不尽に怯えてきた住人の多くが望んでいた姿でもあったろう。
English: This meant that the city had lost something of its character, but it also meant that peace and order had come to it. It was probably the city that many residents, long frightened by all manner of injustice, had wanted.

Japanese: これらはすべて、<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>にかわって<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の<tips=81>龍頭</tips>となった<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の働きによるものだ。彼は<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の圧倒的な組織力を背景に全ての敵対勢力を勢力下に置き、街に安定をもたらした。
English: All this was the work of <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips>, who succeeded <tips=3>Chris Tse</tips> as <tips=81>Longtou</tips> of <tips=7>YS</tips>. Backed by <tips=7>YS's</tips> overwhelming organizational strength, he brought every hostile power under his control and imposed stability on the city.

Japanese: 隣接区域に根を張る<tips=68>木下組</tips>などとの緊張関係はあったが、かつてないほどの強固な組織となった<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>は、彼らの侵入を許すことはない。こうした<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の方針に対し、警察は介入することなく静観の姿勢をとり、事実上黙認した。
English: Tensions remained with the <tips=68>Kinoshita-gumi</tips> and other groups entrenched in neighboring areas, but <tips=7>YS</tips>, now stronger than ever, allowed them no incursion. The police did not intervene in <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> policies, instead standing by and effectively condoning them.

Japanese: この頃、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の影響力は街の隅々にまで及んでいた。
English: By then, <tips=7>YS’s</tips> influence reached into every corner of the city.

Japanese: <tips=9>Y地区</tips>でもっとも危険な地域と言えば<tips=59>暗闇通り</tips>とそこに隣接する貧民街のあたりが有名で、昔から細かい勢力が入り組んでいたが、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>はこれも一掃した。結果として路上で春をひさぐ女は姿を完全に消し、しかるべき店の管理下で営業をするようになった。
English: <tips=59>Darkness Street</tips> and the adjoining slums had long been notorious as the most dangerous part of <tips=9>Y District</tips>, a bewildering tangle of minor powers, but <tips=7>YS</tips> swept those away as well. As a result, women selling themselves vanished completely from the streets and began plying their trade under the management of proper establishments.

Japanese: そして、朝気がつくと正体不明の死体が路地に落ちているということもなくなった。ただ、理由のはっきりとした死体の数は増えた。
English: And unidentified corpses no longer appeared in alleys overnight. The number of corpses with perfectly clear explanations, however, increased.

Japanese: 人種や宗教の違う人々が住む<tips=9>Y地区</tips>で、治安を維持するには結局のところ金と暴力しかない。<tips=1>謝亮</tips>はこれを巧妙に使い、密告社会を作り上げた。
English: In <tips=9>Y District</tips>, home to people of different races and religions, the only means of maintaining order were ultimately money and violence. <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> wielded both with skill and built a society of informants.

Japanese: 例えば裏帳簿を作って<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>への上納金を拒否するもの。例えば外部のギャング組織に通じて私利をむさぼるもの。例えば空き地で遊ぶ子供を捕まえて売り飛ばすもの。<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の方針に逆らう全てのものは密告によって告発され、処刑された。そしてその死体は見せしめのために路上に放置されるのである。
English: Those who kept secret books and refused to pay tribute to <tips=7>YS</tips>. Those who dealt with outside gangs for private gain. Those who seized children playing in vacant lots and sold them. Anyone who defied <tips=7>YS</tips> policy was denounced by informers and executed. The corpses were then left in the street as a warning.

Japanese: 街は清潔になったが、一方で<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>への恐怖は高まっていた。
English: The city grew cleaner, but fear of <tips=7>YS</tips> grew with it.

Japanese: 筆者が訪れた三年前の<tips=9>Y地区</tips>は、まさにそういった状況であった。街が清潔で健全になったかわりに、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の行き過ぎた支配力が空気を息苦しいものにしていた。
English: That was precisely the state of <tips=9>Y District</tips> when the author visited three years ago. The city had become clean and respectable, but in return, <tips=7>YS's</tips> excessive control made the very air oppressive.

Japanese: そのとき私は<tips=58>パラシュート通り</tips>に昔から住む商店主の家を訪ねた。そして、そのリビングルームに<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の肖像が掲げられているのを見つけた。
English: At the time, I visited the home of a shopkeeper who had long lived on <tips=58>Parachute Street</tips>. There, in his living room, I discovered a portrait of <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> on display.

Japanese: こんな趣味の悪いものをどうして飾っているのかと尋ねると、ここだけの秘密だと断ってから、これは魔除けなのだと教えてくれた。
English: When I asked why he displayed something in such dreadful taste, the shopkeeper prefaced his answer by saying it was a secret between us, then explained that the portrait was a charm against evil.

Japanese: 嘘の密告や疑惑をかけられたときのために、日頃からこのようなかたちで<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>への忠誠心をアピールしているのだという。
English: He said he kept the portrait up as a standing display of loyalty to <tips=7>YS</tips>, in case anyone ever made a false report against him or cast suspicion on him.

Japanese: 実際にそのような子供だましが何かの役に立つとも思えなかったし、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の処刑は入念な裏付けのもとに行われていた筈だから、杞憂のようにも思えるが、つまりそれ程に<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>が恐れられているということの証左だった。
English: In fact, it hardly seemed likely that such a childish trick would do any good. Since <tips=7>YS</tips> executions were supposed to be carried out only after meticulous corroboration, the fear seemed needless. Yet the fear itself was evidence of just how deeply <tips=7>YS</tips> was dreaded.

Japanese: ただ、その頃は<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>が恐れられたとは言え、この街は今のように寂れてはいなかったのである。
English: Still, although <tips=7>YS</tips> was feared in those days, the city had not yet fallen into the decline it suffers now.

Japanese: かつてのようなエキゾチックな刺激がなくとも、清潔な、日本のどこにでもある繁華街のように街は栄えていた。
English: Even without the exotic thrills of old, the city prospered as a clean entertainment district like any other in Japan.

Japanese: しかし、それは<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の死と共に崩れた。
English: But it all collapsed with <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> death.

Japanese: 二十一才の時にボスとなった彼は父と同じ難病を患い、まだ若い三十才で一線を退き、そしてその後すぐに死んだ。後継者となったのは<tips=28>トーマス・リャオ</tips>であった。この交代劇が、全てを変えたのだろう。
English: He became boss at twenty-one, developed the same intractable disease as his father, withdrew from the front lines at the still-young age of thirty, and died soon afterward. His successor was <tips=28>Thomas Liao</tips>. That change of leadership was perhaps what changed everything.

Japanese: <tips=28>トーマス</tips>は人望もあり、けして無能なリーダーというわけではなかったが、怜悧で知られた先代ほどには人々に恐れられていなかった。
English: <tips=28>Thomas</tips> was well liked and by no means an incompetent leader, but he inspired less fear than his famously sharp-minded predecessor.

Japanese: そこでどういうことが起きたかというと、<tips=1>謝亮</tips>によって押さえつけられていた不穏分子が、彼がリーダーになったのをきっかけに、再び動き始めたのである。
English: What happened then was that the malcontents <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> had kept suppressed began to stir again when Thomas became leader.

Japanese: まず最初に動いたのは<tips=21>八龍会</tips>だった。
English: The first to move was the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>.

Japanese: 驚くべきことに、十年前の<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>死亡時にすでに老人であった三人の指導者の全員が存命していた。実権を<tips=1>謝亮</tips>に奪われて、ながらく表舞台からは遠ざかっていたが、<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の死後声明を出すと、またたくまに<tips=17>タイプB</tips>たちの支配者の座に返り咲いた。
English: Astonishingly, all three of its leaders—already old men when <tips=3>Chris Tse</tips> died ten years earlier—were still alive. <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> had stripped them of real power, and they had remained out of the public eye for years; but when they issued a declaration after <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> death, they swiftly reclaimed their position as rulers of the <tips=17>Type Bs</tips>.

Japanese: 何の準備もなしに急にそんなことが出来るはずもなく、抜け目のない<tips=22>老人たち</tips>は<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の存命中から工作をしていたのだろう。
English: They could hardly have acted so suddenly without preparation; the shrewd <tips=22>old men</tips> had probably been laying the groundwork while <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> was still alive.

Japanese: とは言え、この時点ではまだ<tips=21>八龍会</tips>は<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>に対し明確に反旗を翻したわけではない。
English: Even so, at this point the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> had not yet openly rebelled against <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: あくまでも<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の一員としての立場を保持したままで、独自の活動を開始したのであった。
English: It began operating independently while still maintaining its position as a member of <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: そして、<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の動きのすぐあとに、もっと重大な事件が起きた。
English: Soon after the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> made its move, an even more momentous event occurred.

Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>のなかから『新義勝』という組織が独立したのだ。
English: An organization called “New Yisheng” broke away from <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: かつてこの街に存在したギャング組織の名をそのまま受け継いだその組織は、かつて<tips=1>謝亮</tips>から疎外された香港人の師弟が中核をなしている。
English: The organization took its name wholesale from a gang that had once existed in the city. At its core were Hong Kong masters and protégés whom <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> had excluded.

Japanese: そのリーダーは<tips=88>アンドリュー・マオ</tips>という二十四歳の青年で、風を操るサイキックであることから『暴風のマオ』と呼ばれていた。
English: Its leader was a twenty-four-year-old man named <tips=88>Andrew Mao</tips>. A psychic able to control wind, he was known as “Mao the Tempest.”

Japanese: 彼は額に第三の目を書き込み、かつての英雄<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>の再来を気取っている。
English: He painted a third eye upon his forehead and posed as the second coming of the old hero <tips=3>Chris Tse</tips>.

Japanese: 彼らの主張はシンプルで、<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の指導によって変化したものを拒否し、彼らが崇拝する<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>初代<tips=81>龍頭</tips>にして未だに語り継がれる英雄<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>の時代に巻き戻そうというものだった。
English: Their demand was simple: reject every change made under <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> and turn the clock back to the age of their idol, <tips=3>Chris Tse</tips>, first <tips=81>Longtou</tips> of <tips=7>YS</tips> and a hero whose legend still endured.

Japanese: この組織が打ち出した思想は、瞬く間に街中に広がり、多くの賛同者を得た。
English: The ideology proclaimed by the organization rapidly spread throughout the city and won a great many adherents.

Japanese: その背景には<tips=88>マオ</tips>を飼い慣らしたい<tips=21>八龍会</tips>の陰謀があったとも、<tips=9>Y地区</tips>内の混乱をもくろむ<tips=68>木下組</tips>の支援があったとも言われているが、それだけでは説明がつかない。やはり、長年抑圧されていた街の人々の心に響いたのだろう。
English: Some said that a conspiracy by the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>, which hoped to tame <tips=88>Mao</tips>, lay behind it; others said it had support from the <tips=68>Kinoshita-gumi</tips>, which hoped to throw <tips=9>Y District</tips> into chaos. But neither explanation was sufficient. Its message must have resonated with people who had endured years of repression.

Japanese: オリジナルの<tips=69>義勝</tips>は香港人以外を受け付けない排他的なものだったが、<tips=88>マオ</tips>が作った新義勝にはそういったこだわりはなく、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>に反発するものなら出身地や肌の色にかかわらず、全てを受け容れた。
English: The original <tips=69>Yisheng</tips> had been an exclusionary organization that accepted no one but Hong Kongers. The New Yisheng created by <tips=88>Mao</tips> had no such fixation: it welcomed anyone opposed to <tips=7>YS</tips>, regardless of birthplace or skin color.

Japanese: そもそも、古い<tips=69>義勝</tips>の時代にあったような、人種的な差別意識というものは、現在のギャング達の間では薄れている。
English: In the first place, the sort of racial prejudice seen in the days of the old <tips=69>Yisheng</tips> has faded among the gangsters of the present day.

Japanese: それは、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>が率先して推し進めた人種・民族の融和方針の結果によるもので、皮肉にもこの方針が敵対組織を強大にしたということになる。
English: This was the result of the policy of racial and ethnic integration that <tips=7>YS</tips> itself had championed. Ironically, that policy had strengthened an enemy organization.

Japanese: ともあれ、数を得た<tips=88>マオ</tips>たちは<tips=28>トーマス</tips>の<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>に敢然と反旗を翻した。
English: In any event, once <tips=88>Mao</tips> and his followers had gained sufficient numbers, they boldly rebelled against <tips=28>Thomas’s</tips> <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: そして、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>と結びつきの強い店舗を襲撃したり、密告者として利益を得ていた人々を誅殺してまわった。
English: They attacked businesses with close ties to <tips=7>YS</tips> and went about executing people who had profited as informers.

Japanese: この<tips=57>滑走路通り</tips>でも何度も暴力事件を起こした。
English: They repeatedly committed acts of violence even here on <tips=57>Runway Street</tips>.

Japanese: そうして治安が悪化すると、<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の代にこの地域に店を出した有名チェーンの店舗などは軒並み閉店し、残ったのは昔からこの街で商売をする、『昔ながらの』ものたちばかりだった。
English: As public safety deteriorated, the famous chains that had opened stores in the district during <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> reign closed one after another. All that remained were the “old-fashioned” merchants who had done business in the city since long ago.

Japanese: 新義勝の、街を古くからの住人の手に取り戻すという目的は、一応達成されたというわけだ。
English: New Yisheng had, after a fashion, achieved its goal of returning the city to its longtime residents.

Japanese: 街が本来の住民の手に戻り、以前のような刺激的な雰囲気を復活させれば、十年前の最盛期のような賑わいが戻るだろう。多少治安が悪くなっても問題はない。実際、かつてはあれだけ危険な場所だったのに人が来ていたのだから。
English: If the city were returned to its original inhabitants and its old, exciting atmosphere restored, the crowds of its heyday ten years ago would return as well. A little deterioration in public safety would be no problem. After all, people had flocked here even when it was every bit as dangerous in the old days.

Japanese: ――というのが<tips=88>アンドリュー・マオ</tips>の理屈だった。
English: —Such was <tips=88>Andrew Mao’s</tips> reasoning.

Japanese: その答え合わせは、すぐに現実的な形で突きつけられることになるのだが。
English: Reality would soon provide a concrete verdict on that prediction.

Japanese: ともあれ、長年街を支配して来た<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>が、得体の知れぬ若者の率いる組織に敗北したというのは衝撃的な事件だった。
English: In any event, it was shocking that <tips=7>YS</tips>, which had ruled the city for years, had been defeated by an organization led by an unknown young man.

Japanese: これをきっかけとして、いくつもの組織が反<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>を表明する。その多くは<tips=1>謝亮</tips>時代には、当時の<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の圧倒的な勢力に屈し、不本意ながら従っていた——つまりもともと友好的とは言えない組織だが、反目したのはそうした元々忠誠心の低い外部組織だけではない。
English: That defeat prompted numerous organizations to declare themselves against <tips=7>YS</tips>. Most had submitted reluctantly to <tips=7>YS’s</tips> overwhelming power under <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips>—organizations that had never been particularly friendly in the first place. But the opposition was not confined to such outside groups, whose loyalty had always been weak.

Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>内部からも、いくつもの対立組織が生まれた。<tips=28>トーマス・リャオ</tips>のやり方に疑問を持った有力者たちが、次々と独立したのである。
English: Several rival organizations also emerged within <tips=7>YS</tips>. Powerful figures who questioned <tips=28>Thomas Liao’s</tips> methods broke away one after another.

Japanese: なかでも一番街の人々を驚かせたのは、<tips=85>二路元帥</tips><tips=25>馬世傑</tips>の離反だった。
English: What astonished the people of the city most of all was the defection of <tips=85>Second Route Marshal</tips> <tips=25>Ma Sai-kit</tips>.

Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>を築いた立役者の一人である<tips=4>馬明</tips>の息子にして、<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の懐刀でもあった彼は、争いの場では常に積極的に指揮を執っていた。<tips=81>龍頭</tips>の無二の親友であり、最良の部下であると、誰もが認めていた彼の独立は誰にも予期が出来なかった。
English: The son of <tips=4>Ma Ming</tips>, one of the chief architects of <tips=7>YS</tips>, and <tips=1>Tse Leung's</tips> right-hand man, he had always taken an active command role whenever conflict arose. Everyone regarded him as the <tips=81>Longtou's</tips> closest friend and finest subordinate. No one could have anticipated that he would break away.

Japanese: <tips=25>馬世傑</tips>を支えたのは父<tips=4>馬明</tips>のかつての部下だけでない。穏健派の<tips=28>トーマス・リャオ</tips>の平和的なやり方にどうしても賛同出来ないものたちも、彼の下に集った。
English: It was not only his father <tips=4>Ma Ming's</tips> former subordinates who supported <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips>. Those who could not bring themselves to accept the peaceful methods of the moderate <tips=28>Thomas Liao</tips> also rallied to him.

Japanese: その数は<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>全体の規模からすればさほど多いとは言えなかったが、優秀な<tips=17>タイプB</tips>やサイキックなど若手の実力者ばかりだっため、すぐに無視が出来ない勢力となった。
English: Their numbers were not especially large compared with <tips=7>YS</tips> as a whole, but they were all formidable young figures—gifted <tips=17>Type Bs</tips>, psychics, and the like—and they quickly became a power no one could ignore.

Japanese: 名誉や富に何の関心も持っていないと思われていた<tips=25>馬世傑</tips>が、このように独立した理由は、今一つはっきりしない。
English: Why <tips=25>Ma Sai-kit</tips>, who had seemed indifferent to honor and wealth, chose to break away remained unclear.

Japanese: 素直に組織に居座っていたほうが、もっと大きな権力を手に入れられたはずなのだ。かつて父を<tips=1>謝亮</tips>に殺されたことを恨みに思っているという説もあるが、噂の域を出ない。
English: He could surely have acquired greater power by simply remaining inside the organization. One theory held that he resented <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> for killing his father, but it had never risen above rumor.

Japanese: 彼はどうやらサイキックであるらしいが、その能力の詳細は明らかにされてはいなかった。
English: He was apparently a psychic, but the details of his ability had never been disclosed.

Japanese: 何もかもが謎に包まれている。
English: Everything about him was shrouded in mystery.

Japanese: しかし、その正体がどうあれ、彼の独立が<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の力を削ぎ、この街に群雄割拠の時代をもたらしたことは確かだ。
English: But whatever his true nature, his secession indisputably weakened <tips=7>YS</tips> and ushered in an age of rival warlords within the city.

Japanese: <tips=25>馬世傑</tips>のグループは、独立はしたものの、いまのところはまだ<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>とあからさまに敵対しているわけではない。
English: Although <tips=25>Ma Sai-kit’s</tips> group had become independent, for now it was not yet openly hostile toward <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: <tips=88>マオ</tips>の新義勝とも距離を置き、沈黙を保っている。しかし、彼らと同じ道を行くつもりはなさそうだ。
English: It also kept its distance from <tips=88>Mao’s</tips> New Yisheng and remained silent. It did not, however, appear inclined to follow the same path.

Japanese: <tips=25>馬世傑</tips>が何を考えているのか、その組織が今後どういった方針をとるのかは不明だが、その動向は他の全ての組織にとって重要なものとなるだろう。
English: What <tips=25>Ma Sai-kit</tips> was thinking and what course his organization would take remained unknown, but its movements would matter to every other organization.

Japanese: さて、そうして重要な人員を、まるで櫛の歯を引くように失っていった<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>は、当然のことながら、その運営は困難を極めている。
English: With key personnel disappearing one after another, leaving gaps like missing teeth in a comb, <tips=7>YS</tips> naturally found itself extraordinarily difficult to run.

Japanese: 先代<tips=1>謝亮</tips>と同じように、就任直後に難しい状況に立たされた新<tips=81>龍頭</tips><tips=28>トーマス</tips>は、彼の穏健な性格どおり当初は平和的な交渉で解決を試みたのだが、これはかえって敵対者を調子づかせ、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>からの離反をさらに作り出すきっかけとなった。
English: Like <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> before him, the new <tips=81>Longtou</tips> <tips=28>Thomas</tips> inherited a difficult situation the moment he took office. True to his moderate nature, he initially tried to resolve it through peaceful negotiation. That only emboldened his enemies and prompted still more defections from <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: <tips=28>トーマス</tips>は穏健派ではあったが、事態がこうまで収拾のつかないものになってしまうと、そうも言っていられない。結局、暴力を用いるほかなくなる。
English: <tips=28>Thomas</tips> was a moderate, but with the situation this far beyond control, moderation was no longer an option. In the end, he had no choice but to resort to violence.

Japanese: まず、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>内の大規模な粛清を行った。
English: First, he conducted a large-scale purge within <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: 新義勝やら<tips=68>木下組</tips>やらと通じてスパイとなったものが、この混乱に乗じて大量に発生していたため、一掃しなければまともに組織が動かない状況にまで陥っていたのだ。
English: So many people had taken advantage of the confusion to become spies for New Yisheng, the <tips=68>Kinoshita-gumi</tips>, and other groups that the organization could no longer function properly unless they were swept away.

Japanese: ただ、このスパイの検出はあまり精度の高いものではなかった。結果として何の罪もないメンバーが殺害されることになり、事態は凄惨を極めた。この粛清事件は組織の内外から大きな反発を呼び、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>への非難の声明を出す組織が次々と現れ、この街での武力闘争はますます本格化してゆくのである。
English: The methods used to identify these spies were not particularly accurate, however. Innocent members were killed as a result, and the situation became ghastly. The purge provoked fierce opposition both inside and outside the organization. Group after group issued statements condemning <tips=7>YS</tips>, and the armed struggle within the city grew ever more intense.

Japanese: このあたりの経緯は、<tips=3>クリス・ツェー</tips>死後の抗争と似ている。
English: The course of events resembled the conflict that followed <tips=3>Chris Tse’s</tips> death.

Japanese: 歴史は繰り返すと言うとおり、これも避け得ない運命だったのだろう。
English: History repeats itself, as the saying goes, and perhaps this too was an inescapable fate.

Japanese: 当時混乱を巻き起こすきっかけとなったのが<tips=81>龍頭</tips>の地位を狙う<tips=27>廖志明</tips>の野望だったことを思うと、その息子の<tips=28>トーマス</tips>が逆に<tips=81>龍頭</tips>として組織を守る立場になったのは皮肉なものだ。
English: When one considers that the earlier chaos was triggered by <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming’s</tips> ambition to claim the position of <tips=81>Longtou</tips>, there was a certain irony in his son <tips=28>Thomas</tips> now defending the organization as its <tips=81>Longtou</tips>.

Japanese: ちなみに、この<tips=27>廖志明</tips>は<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の死後は街に戻って、<tips=28>トーマス</tips>の補佐をしている。彼自身も、今度は<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>を守る立場で反逆者たちと戦うことになったというわけだ。
English: Incidentally, <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips> returned to the city after <tips=1>Tse Leung's</tips> death and is now assisting <tips=28>Thomas</tips>. This time, he too has found himself fighting rebels from the position of defending <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: さて、現在は<tips=1>謝亮</tips>が死んで一年がすぎている。
English: Now, one year has passed since <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> death.

Japanese: ギャングたちの抗争は、まだ終わってはいない。どころか、ますます過激さを増している。
English: The gang war is not yet over. Far from it: it is growing ever more violent.

Japanese: 先日も<tips=88>マオ</tips>の新義勝と、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の大規模な激突があり、多くの死者が出たばかりだ。
English: Only the other day, <tips=88>Mao’s</tips> New Yisheng and <tips=7>YS</tips> clashed on a massive scale, leaving many dead.

Japanese: そして、この一年の間に<tips=57>滑走路通り</tips>はこんなにも変化してしまった。<tips=88>マオ</tips>の目論んだような、最盛期の繁栄は戻っては来なかった。<tips=1>謝亮</tips>の統治下で一時期姿を消していた浮浪者たちはまた路上に姿をあらわし、出店したチェーン店は全て撤退し、このような時間でも人気の少ない寂れた街になってしまったのである。
English: And in the space of this one year, <tips=57>Runway Street</tips> had changed beyond recognition. The prosperity of its heyday—the prosperity <tips=88>Mao</tips> had envisioned—never returned. Vagrants who had briefly vanished under <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> rule reappeared on the streets, every chain store that had opened pulled out, and the district became a desolate place with few people about even at this hour.

Japanese: もちろん、こうなれば警察も黙ってはいなかった。
English: Of course, once matters reached this point, the police did not sit idle.

Japanese: しかし、事態はあまりにも混沌としている。警察は介入の手段を見つけ出すため、まず徹底した調査を行うこととした。その結果として、以前<tips=9>Y地区</tips>でのゴタゴタのなかで、警察と関わりを持ったことがある筆者のもとにも、街の情勢を調査してくれないかという依頼が届いたのである。
English: The situation was far too chaotic, however. To find some means of intervening, the police first decided to conduct a thorough investigation. As a result, a request to investigate conditions in the city reached the author as well, since he had dealt with the police during an earlier disturbance in <tips=9>Y District</tips>.

Japanese: というわけで、筆者がいまこの街を歩いているのは、警察からの依頼によるものだった。
English: That, then, was why the author was now walking through the city: he was here at the request of the police.

Japanese: 先月から<tips=9>Y地区</tips>に滞在し、主に新義勝についての調査活動を行っている。
English: The author has been staying in <tips=9>Y District</tips> since last month, chiefly to investigate New Yisheng.

Japanese: しかし、街に来てすぐに後悔した。筆者はこの街で生まれ育ったが、十年前に個人的な事情があって街を捨てている。ひさしぶりに戻って滞在をし、街の風景を眺めていると、いやなことばかり思い出して仕方ない。
English: But the author regretted coming almost at once. He had been born and raised in this city, but abandoned it ten years ago for personal reasons. Returning after so long and spending his days among its streets, he found unpleasant memories surfacing one after another, whether he wanted them to or not.

Japanese: さっさと仕事を片付けて街を出るつもりだったのだが、調査を始めて半月ほど過ぎたころ、その仕事への取り組み方を変えさせる出来事があった。
English: I had intended to finish the work quickly and leave the city, but about half a month into the investigation, something happened that changed how I approached the job.

Japanese: 街は全体に寂れているが、<tips=57>滑走路通り</tips>の北の方だけは今も少し栄えている。そこには酒を飲ませる古い店が立ちならび、かつて私がよく通った飲食店も健在だった。
English: The city as a whole had declined, but the northern end of <tips=57>Runway Street</tips> still retained some prosperity. Old establishments serving alcohol stood in a row there, and one restaurant I had often frequented remained in business.

Japanese: ——そこで酒を飲んだ帰りである。
English: —I was on my way back from drinking there.

Japanese: 「おい、おまえ！」
English: “Hey, you!”

Japanese: 背後から女の声がしたが、振り向いても誰もいない。
English: A woman’s voice came from behind me, but when I turned, no one was there.

Japanese: 「こっちだ、こっち」
English: “Up here. Up here.”

Japanese: 声は上の方からきこえた。
English: The voice came from above.

Japanese: 顎をあげてそちらを見ると、この街特有の雲で覆われた真っ暗な夜空を背景に、女が浮かんでいる。
English: I raised my chin and looked. A woman floated against the utterly black night sky, blanketed by the clouds peculiar to this city.

Japanese: その女は、黒い服を着て、そして両手には物騒なものを抱えていた。
English: The woman was dressed in black and cradled something dangerous in both hands.

Japanese: 闇の中に黒くくすんだそれを、目を細めて識別する。
English: Squinting, I made out its dark, dull shape against the night.

Japanese: 確かこれは『AN-94』。ロシア製のアサルトライフルで、最近<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>がよく用いているものだ。
English: An AN-94, if I remembered correctly—a Russian-made assault rifle recently favored by <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: 「お前、最近この街をこそこそと調べ回っているそうじゃないか」
English: “I hear you’ve been sneaking around this city investigating things lately.”

Japanese: 女の顔は、電灯の光で鈍く光っている。何か表面が濡れているらしい。
English: The woman's face glistened dully in the streetlight. Some wet substance appeared to be clinging to its surface.

Japanese: 汗と言うよりも、もっと粘土のあるものが肌に張り付いている。年齢は二十代後半といったところか。
English: It was not sweat, but something more viscous clinging to her skin. She looked to be in her late twenties.

Japanese: 筆者はこの人物とは面識こそないものの、心当たりがあった。
English: The author had never met this woman, but he had a good idea who she might be.

Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>には空を自由に飛び回る女のサイキックがいるという。新義勝との抗争にもしばしば姿を現し、その飛行能力と優れた銃の腕前で恐れられているそうだ。
English: The author had heard that <tips=7>YS</tips> had a female psychic who could fly freely through the air. She was said to appear often in its clashes with New Yisheng and to be feared for both her power of flight and her superb marksmanship.

Japanese: 「『<tips=51>サクラ</tips>』か」
English: “<tips=51>Sakura</tips>?”

Japanese: 筆者が名を呼んでも、相手は顔色一つ変えない。
English: The woman showed no reaction when the author spoke her name.

Japanese: 「その気持ち悪い覆面をとれ。顔を見せろ」
English: “Take off that revolting mask. Show me your face.”

Japanese: 彼女は銃口をこちらに向けている。引き金に指をかけ、今にも撃ちそうな剣幕だ。
English: She had the muzzle trained on me, her finger on the trigger, and looked ready to fire at any moment.

Japanese: 筆者は特殊な体質があり、もし撃たれたところで大したことはないのだが、騒ぎを起こしたくなかったので、大人しくその言葉に従った。
English: The author possessed an unusual constitution, so being shot would have done him little harm. He did not want to cause a disturbance, however, and quietly complied.

Japanese: 「名前を言え」
English: “Tell me your name.”

Japanese: 覆面をとって素顔になった筆者に彼女は命令をする。
English: She issued the command once the author had removed his mask and exposed his face.

Japanese: 「<tips=50>路地邦昭</tips>……元探偵だ」
English: “<tips=50>Kuniaki Roji</tips>... Former detective.”

Japanese: と、私は言った。
English: I answered.

Japanese: 「探偵の<tips=50>路地</tips>？　知ってるぞ。でも、そいつはとっくに街から消えたと聞いている。それに、<tips=50>路地</tips>と言えば角が生えた鬼のような男として有名だったはずじゃないか。角はどこにある？　隠しているようには見えないぞ」
English: “<tips=50>Roji</tips> the detective? I’ve heard of him. But I heard he left the city long ago. And wasn’t <tips=50>Roji</tips> famous as a demon of a man with horns? Where are your horns? You don’t seem to be hiding any.”

Japanese: 「今は街の外でノーマルに混じって暮らしているから、目立ちたくないのさ」
English: “I live outside the city now, among the Normals, and I don’t want to draw attention.”

Japanese: 私は前髪をめくって、角を切断した痕を見せる。
English: I swept back my bangs and showed her the scars where my horns had been cut away.

Japanese: 「毎日削らなきゃすぐに伸びてくる。面倒なものだ」
English: “They grow back almost at once unless I file them down every day. A tiresome business.”

Japanese: 「……その元探偵が、今ここで何をしている？」
English: “...And what is a former detective doing here now?”

Japanese: 少し迷ったが、私は正直に言うことにした。
English: After a moment’s hesitation, I decided to tell her the truth.

Japanese: 「警察に依頼されて調査しているんだよ。銃を下げた方がいい。ここでお前がおれを撃てばややこしくなる」
English: “The police hired me to investigate. You should lower the gun. If you shoot me here, matters will become complicated.”

Japanese: 私の言葉に<tips=51>サクラ</tips>は露骨に迷いを見せた。
English: <tips=51>Sakura</tips> showed open hesitation at my words.

Japanese: 警察と<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>は表面上はまだ協力関係にある。<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>に所属する彼女が、警察の依頼を受けて活動をしている私に危害を加えれば面倒なことになるのは理解しているだろうが、私の言葉を信じ切れないのだ。
English: The police and <tips=7>YS</tips> still maintained an outwardly cooperative relationship. She probably understood that if she, a member of <tips=7>YS</tips>, harmed me while I was working at the police’s request, it would cause trouble. Yet she could not bring herself to trust what I said completely.

Japanese: 「証拠を見せてやる。……撃つなよ」
English: “I’ll show you proof. ...Don’t shoot.”

Japanese: 私はそう警告してからジャケットの内側に手を突っ込み、一枚のカードを取り出して彼女に見せた。
English: After giving that warning, I slipped a hand inside my jacket, withdrew a card, and held it out for her to see.

Japanese: それは、公的機関に協力するサイキックに与えられる身分証で、本来ならば禁止されているサイキック能力を限定的に使用出来る許可証でもある。この国に暮らすサイキックなら誰でも喉から手が出るほど欲しいしろもので、当然<tips=51>サクラ</tips>もそのデザインに見覚えがあるだろう。
English: It was identification issued to psychics who assisted public institutions, and also a special permit authorizing limited use of psychic abilities that were ordinarily forbidden. Any psychic living in this country would have killed for one, and <tips=51>Sakura</tips> was bound to recognize the design.

Japanese: 「……わかった」
English: “...All right.”

Japanese: <tips=51>サクラ</tips>は銃を下ろす。そしてそのまま飛び去ろうとしたのだが、
English: <tips=51>Sakura</tips> lowered the rifle and was about to fly off, but—

Japanese: 「おい」
English: “Hey.”

Japanese: 私はそれを呼び止めた。
English: I called after her.

Japanese: 「ちょっと話を聞かせてくれ。知りたいことがあるんだ。話してくれたら、私が新義勝について調べたいくつかの事実を、特別に教えてやろう」
English: “Talk to me for a moment. There’s something I want to know. If you tell me, I’ll let you in on a few things I uncovered about New Yisheng.”

Japanese: 「……組織のことは何も話す事が出来ない」
English: “...I can’t tell you anything about the organization.”

Japanese: 「<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>のことは聞かない。私が知りたいのは、<tips=31>エリー・ホワイト</tips>のことだ」
English: “I won’t ask about <tips=7>YS</tips>. I want to know about <tips=31>Ellie White</tips>.”

Japanese: 私の言葉に迷いを見せてから、
English: She hesitated at my words.

Japanese: 「わかった」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: <tips=51>サクラ</tips>はそう頷いた。
English: <tips=51>Sakura</tips> nodded.

Everyone in this world of killing and being killed is mad. In the end, people like us always meet with some fate that makes the accounts balance. That’s the rule here. But you shouldn’t have to submit to this world’s rules just yet.”

Japanese: 「私だって、後戻りなんか出来ません」
English: “It is too late for me to turn back, too.”

Japanese: 「そうかしら。死ぬのはこわいでしょう？」
English: “Are you sure? You’re afraid to die, aren’t you?”

Japanese: <tips=38>リタ</tips>は何か言いかけるが、それは言葉にならず、俯く。
English: <tips=38>Rita</tips> began to say something, but no words emerged. She lowered her head.

Japanese: その様子を見て<tips=25>世傑</tips>は苦笑し、
English: <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips> watched her and gave a rueful smile.

Japanese: 「ねえあなた、<tips=2>阿亮</tips>のことが好きだったんでしょ？」
English: “Tell me. You were in love with <tips=2>Ah Leung</tips>, weren’t you?”

Japanese: 唐突にそう訊ねた。
English: The question came without warning.

Japanese: 「そ、そんな……」
English: “Th-that’s not...”

Japanese: <tips=38>リタ</tips>は慌てて否定したが、その言葉とは裏腹に顔はみるみるうちに赤くなる。
English: <tips=38>Rita</tips> hurried to deny it, but even as she spoke, her face flushed deeper and deeper.

Japanese: 「だったら、<tips=2>阿亮</tips>と今度こそ本当に結婚しなさいよ。アタシが仲介するわ」
English: “Then marry <tips=2>Ah Leung</tips> for real this time. I’ll arrange it.”

Japanese: 「む、無理です。それは……」
English: “I-I can’t. That would...”

Japanese: 「それはあなたのためじゃなくて、<tips=2>阿亮</tips>のためにも。今の彼には支えが必要なの」
English: “And not just for your sake—for <tips=2>Ah Leung’s</tips> as well. He needs someone to support him now.”

Japanese: 「……大丈夫ですよ。あの人は強い人です」
English: “...He will be all right. He is a strong man.”

Japanese: <tips=38>リタ</tips>は首を横に振る。
English: <tips=38>Rita</tips> shook her head.

Japanese: 「アタシは色んな人を見たけど、本当に強い人なんか世界には一人もいないわ。みんなやせ我慢をしてるだけよ」
English: “I have seen all kinds of people, and there isn’t one truly strong person in this world. Everyone is only putting up a brave front.”

Japanese: 「そうかもしれませんが、私には無理です」
English: “Perhaps. But I cannot do this.”

Japanese: 「死んだお姉さんたちが反対していたから？」
English: “Because your dead sisters opposed it?”

Japanese: 「違います！」
English: “No!”

Japanese: <tips=38>リタ</tips>は突然顔を上げて抗議をしたが、すぐに大声を恥じて元のように俯き、
English: <tips=38>Rita</tips> suddenly raised her head in protest. Almost at once, embarrassed by her own loud voice, she looked down again.

Japanese: 「確かに昔は好きだったかもしれません。でも、いまは違います。……私はあの人に認められたいんです。一人前の人間として。だから、もうこの話は終わりです」
English: “Perhaps I did like him once. But I don’t anymore. ...I want that man to acknowledge me—as an adult in my own right. So this conversation is over.”

Japanese: 「<tips=38>リタ</tips>ちゃん。それはね……」
English: “<tips=38>Rita</tips>. That is...”

Japanese: 言いかけた<tips=25>世傑</tips>の言葉を遮って、
English: Rita cut off whatever <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips> had been about to say.

Japanese: 「すみませんが、出て行ってください」
English: “I’m sorry, but please leave.”

Japanese: 「わかったわ」
English: “All right.”

Japanese: <tips=25>世傑</tips>はなおも何か言いたそうだったが、<tips=38>リタ</tips>の固い横顔を見て諦めたようだった。
English: <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips> still looked as though he wanted to say more, but the resolve in <tips=38>Rita’s</tips> profile made him think better of it.

Japanese: 相手の手を離し、立ち上がる。
English: He released her hand and rose.

Japanese: 「じゃあ、おやすみ」
English: “Good night, then.”

Japanese: パチリと照明を落として、ドアを閉めようとしたその時、
English: He switched off the light with a click and had begun closing the door when—

Japanese: 「<tips=25>世傑</tips>さん」
English: “<tips=25>Sai-kit</tips>.”

Japanese: と<tips=38>リタ</tips>が呼びかけた。
English: <tips=38>Rita</tips> called out to him.

Japanese: 「私、死ぬつもりなんかありません。絶対に相手をやっつけて、生き延びるんですから。そうしたら、次のことを考えます。だからその時は、私に協力してくださいね」
English: “I have no intention of dying. I will defeat them, and I will survive. Then I will decide what comes next. So when that time comes, please help me.”

Japanese: その声は、最後は泣き声になっていた。
English: By the end, her voice had broken into a sob.

Japanese: 「わかったわ。その時は、なんだってしてあげちゃうんだから……」
English: “All right. When the time comes, I’ll do absolutely anything for you...”

Japanese: 言った<tips=25>世傑</tips>の声も震えている。
English: <tips=25>Sai-kit’s</tips> voice was trembling now, too.

Japanese: 「おやすみ」
English: “Good night.”

Japanese: <tips=25>世傑</tips>は自分の表情を見せまいと、ドアを閉めた。そしてそのドアを背に目元を抑えた時、背後から<tips=38>リタ</tips>のすすり泣く嗚咽が聞こえた。
English: <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips> closed the door to keep her from seeing his expression. Then, with his back to the door, he pressed a hand to his eyes and heard <tips=38>Rita</tips> sobbing behind him.

Japanese: 翌朝すぐに<tips=38>リタ・フェルナンデス</tips>はマンションを出て行った。
English: <tips=38>Rita Fernandes</tips> left the apartment early the next morning.

Japanese: 親戚の家に到着した<tips=38>リタ</tips>はその日のうちに自分の生存をインターネット上に表明し、そして<tips=21>八龍会</tips>を非難した。
English: After reaching her relatives’ home, <tips=38>Rita</tips> announced online that same day that she was alive, and denounced the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips>.

Japanese: これによって<tips=75>フェルナンデス・ファミリー</tips>と<tips=21>八龍会</tips>が完全に対立するかたちとなったわけだが、しかし抗争が本格化する前に<tips=17>タイプB</tips>の青年二人の裏切りによって<tips=38>リタ</tips>とその親戚は殺害される。
English: The <tips=75>Fernandes Family</tips> and the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> were thereby placed in open opposition. Before the conflict could escalate in earnest, however, <tips=38>Rita</tips> and her relatives were murdered after two young <tips=17>Type B</tips> men betrayed them.

Japanese: 裏切り者たちは<tips=38>リタ</tips>の首を切り取り、それを手土産に<tips=47>解放軍</tips>に駆け込むと、<tips=47>解放軍</tips>はその加入を快く受け入れた。
English: The traitors cut off <tips=38>Rita’s</tips> head and carried it as an offering when they sought refuge with the <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips>. The <tips=47>Liberation Army</tips> welcomed them gladly into its ranks.

Japanese: その後、かつてフェルナンデス家を襲撃した若者たちがされたように、<tips=38>リタ</tips>と彼女を匿った人々の遺体は<tips=59>暗闇通り</tips>の路地に放置された。
English: Afterward, the bodies of <tips=38>Rita</tips> and the people who had sheltered her were abandoned in an alley off <tips=59>Darkness Street</tips>—the same treatment once given to the young men who had attacked the Fernandes family.

Japanese: 衣服を剥がれたそのいたましい遺体は通行人に撮影され、<tips=9>Y地区</tips>の暗部を示す一シーンとして週刊誌の一面を飾ることになる。
English: Passersby photographed the tragic, naked bodies, and one such image later filled the front page of a weekly magazine as a tableau of <tips=9>Y District’s</tips> dark underbelly.

Japanese: このとき<tips=38>リタ・フェルナンデス</tips>はわずか１９才だった。
English: <tips=38>Rita Fernandes</tips> was only nineteen years old.

Japanese: <tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の<tips=81>龍頭</tips><tips=1>謝亮</tips>は報告を受けるとすぐに部下をその現場に派遣し、かつては盟友であった少女とその親族の遺体を回収すると、先に死んだ家族たちのそばに埋葬した。
English: Upon receiving the report, <tips=7>YS’s</tips> <tips=81>Longtou</tips>, <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips>, immediately sent subordinates to the site. They recovered the bodies of the girl who had once been his ally and of her relatives, then buried them beside the members of her family who had died before them.

Japanese: こうして、<tips=9>Y地区</tips>で有数の勢力を持っていた<tips=75>フェルナンデス・ファミリー</tips>を完全な壊滅状態においやったことで、<tips=21>八龍会</tips>は名実ともに<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>に対抗しうる存在として周知されることになった。
English: By bringing the <tips=75>Fernandes Family</tips>—once one of the dominant powers in <tips=9>Y District</tips>—to total ruin, the <tips=21>Eight Dragons Society</tips> established itself beyond dispute as an organization capable of challenging <tips=7>YS</tips>.

Japanese: <tips=9>Y地区</tips>の西側には朽ちかけたトタンやシミのついた板キレなど、あり合わせのもので作り上げた粗末な簡易住宅が並ぶ地域がある。
English: On the western side of <tips=9>Y District</tips> lay a neighborhood of wretched makeshift homes cobbled together from whatever came to hand: rotting sheets of tin, stained scraps of wood, and the like.

Japanese: そこに住む人は貧しくはあるが賑やかで、路上では子供たちが声をあげながらボール遊びに興じていたり、生きた鶏をしめる老人の周りには少しでも肉を安く買おうと人が集まり、太った女たちは煙草を吸いながら立ち話をしている。また別の片隅では中年の男たちが輪になって座り込み、大麻を回して吸っている。
English: The people who lived there were poor but lively. Children shouted as they played ball in the streets; people hoping to buy meat a little cheaper gathered around an old man slaughtering live chickens; heavyset women stood smoking and talking; and elsewhere, circles of middle-aged men sat in the street passing marijuana around.

Japanese: 彼らが貧しいのは仕事にありつけないからではなく、働く意欲が低いのだ。
English: They were poor not because they could not find work, but because they had little inclination to work.

Japanese: 金がなくなれば<tips=57>滑走路通り</tips>だの繁華街の方へ行ってアルバイトをしたり、もう少し度胸のあるものはひったくりや万引きなどをするのだが、多少でも小金があれば何もせずにだらだらと路上で時間を過ごしている。
English: When they ran out of money, they went to <tips=57>Runway Street</tips> or the entertainment district and picked up odd jobs; the slightly bolder among them turned to purse-snatching or shoplifting. But as long as they had a little cash in hand, they did nothing and idled away the hours in the street.

Japanese: 肌の色も顔立ちもまちまちで、混血児も多く、国籍も定かではないが、路上の人々はみな明るく陽気で、その日を楽しんで暮らしていた。
English: Their skin colors and features varied widely, many were of mixed descent, and their nationalities were uncertain. Yet the people in the streets were all bright and cheerful, enjoying each day as it came.

Japanese: もちろん、表情が明るいからといって彼らの心が満たされているというわけでもなく、希望から見放された者たち特有のある種軽薄な明るさと、人間が本質的にもつ楽観的な明るさの両方が複雑に入り交じったものではあったが。
English: Of course, their bright expressions did not mean they felt fulfilled. Their cheer was a complex mixture: the peculiar frivolity of people abandoned by hope, mingled with the optimism inherent in human nature.

Japanese: いかにも<tips=9>Y地区</tips>らしいこの地域の一角、雑木林に隔てられたところに、周囲の住宅とは一線を画す堅牢なコンクリートの壁で囲まれた城のように巨大な建築物があった。
English: Beyond a thicket in one corner of this quintessentially <tips=9>Y District</tips> neighborhood stood an enormous, castle-like building. Stout concrete walls set it sharply apart from the homes around it.

Japanese: 出入り口は正門と裏の通用門の二つがあり、いずれの門にも警備員が張り付き、入ろうとする者だけでなく、出ようとするものに対しても厳しい選別を行っている。彼らの態度をつぶさに観察すると、むしろ塀の内側、中から外に出ようとするものに対する警戒の方が強いと感じられるかもしれない。
English: It had two entrances, a main gate and a service gate at the rear. Guards stood watch at both, subjecting those who tried to leave to the same strict scrutiny as those who sought to enter. Anyone who watched them closely might even conclude that they were more wary of people trying to pass from inside the walls to the world beyond.

Japanese: 門に掛かる表札には、<tips=6>国立巻河原病院</tips>とある。しかし、世間ではあまりそうは呼ばれない。
English: The plaque on the gate bore the name <tips=6>National Makigawara Hospital</tips>. But that was rarely what people called it.

Japanese: 『<tips=6>タイプＢ収容所</tips>』
English: ‘The <tips=6>Type B Internment Center</tips>.’

Japanese: そんなおどろおどろしい通称で呼ばれることが、ほとんどであろう。
English: It was almost always known by that ominous nickname.

Japanese: その歴史は古い。
English: It had a long history.

Japanese: 基地が取り壊された直後の、更地のなかに置き捨てられた廃墟がぽつりぽつりと目に付くような、まるで人気のない土地にこの病院は建設された。
English: The hospital had been built just after the base was demolished, on virtually deserted land where abandoned ruins still dotted the cleared lots.

Japanese: つまり、この病院は街が出来るよりも前に建設されたということだ。
English: In other words, the hospital had been built before the town itself.

Japanese: 雑然としたスラム街に病院を建設したのではなく、先に病院が出来てから、まわりの空き地に勝手にうろんな人々が住み着いたのである。
English: The hospital had not been built in the middle of a ramshackle slum. It came first; only afterward had dubious characters simply moved onto the vacant land around it.

Japanese: 塀の中には五つの建物があった。
English: There were five buildings inside the walls.

Japanese: そのうち三つは患者たちが暮らす病棟。
English: Three of them were wards where the patients lived.

Japanese: もう一つはOT棟と呼ばれており、作業療法室、図書室、ビデオ視聴室などがある。
English: Another was called the OT Building and contained an occupational-therapy room, a library, a video room, and other facilities.

Japanese: そして、最後の一つは医局や事務室などがある管理棟となっていた。
English: The fifth was the Administration Building, which housed the physicians’ offices, administrative offices, and other departments.

Japanese: 建物の間の空間は運動場となっており、雨に打たれて錆だらけになったバスケットボールのゴールが見える。
English: The spaces between the buildings served as exercise yards. Basketball hoops stood there, eaten through with rust from years in the rain.

Japanese: この病院は、<tips=17>タイプB</tips>専門病院である。
English: This hospital specialized exclusively in <tips=17>Type B</tips> patients.

Japanese: 患者たちはその症状の内容や性別によって、それぞれの病棟に振り分けられている。
English: Patients were assigned to the various wards according to the nature of their symptoms and their sex.

Japanese: たとえば比較的症状の軽い女性患者はB病棟の一階で暮らし、病院内の施設を自由に利用することが出来る。急性期で症状が安定しないが集団生活を営める状態である男性患者はA病棟の二階で暮らし、棟の外に出る扉には鍵がかけられている。
English: Female patients with comparatively mild symptoms, for example, lived on the first floor of Ward B and could use the hospital’s facilities freely. Male patients in the acute phase whose symptoms remained unstable, but who could still tolerate communal living, lived on the second floor of Ward A. The door leading out of that building was kept locked.

Japanese: <tips=83>能見美紗</tips>が勤務しているのは、B病棟の三階だ。
English: <tips=83>Misa Nomi</tips> worked on the third floor of Ward B.

Japanese: 症状が慢性化し、状態が安定しているものの軽度とは言えない女性患者たちが暮らす閉鎖病棟であった。
English: It was a locked ward for female patients whose conditions, though chronic and stable, could not be described as mild.

Japanese: <tips=83>美紗</tips>は二十六才のまだ若い看護師だが、なぜこんな施設で働くことになってしまったのかと、時に自分の人生を不思議に思う。
English: At twenty-six, <tips=83>Misa</tips> was still a young nurse. Sometimes she found herself wondering how on earth her life had brought her to work in a place like this.

Japanese: 親の入院を見舞いに行った時、看護師の優しい振る舞いと、てきぱきと働くさまにいたく感動した、というエピソードは少女が看護師になる理由としてはごく平凡なものだろう。
English: A girl visits a hospitalized parent and is deeply moved by the nurses’ kindness and brisk competence: as reasons for becoming a nurse went, it was an utterly ordinary story.

Japanese: だが実際看護師になって、就職先を探す時、必ずしも希望通りの診療科に配属されるとは限らないものだ。
English: But even after becoming a nurse and finding a job, there was no guarantee that she would be assigned to the department she wanted.

Japanese: しかし、あまりにも<tips=97>特殊なタイプＢ</tips>専用病棟――しかも悪名高い『<tips=6>タイプＢ収容所</tips>』に勤務することになるというのは、看護学生であった頃の<tips=83>美紗</tips>の想像のなかにはまったく存在しなかった。
English: Yet the idea that she would end up working in a ward exclusively for <tips=97>special Type Bs</tips>—and at the infamous ‘<tips=6>Type B Internment Center</tips>,’ no less—had never once entered <tips=83>Misa’s</tips> imagination when she was a nursing student.

Japanese: この病院は、よその病院で面倒を見切れなくなった患者や、社会で問題を起こして行政によって強制的に入院させられた患者などを積極的に受け入れている。
English: The hospital actively took in patients other hospitals had given up trying to manage, along with people who had caused trouble in society and been committed by the authorities.

Japanese: <tips=17>タイプB</tips>は基本的に一度精神症状が出てしまったら完治することはない。しかも、彼らはその異常な身体能力のために、収容する病棟には特別な設備が必要となる。
English: As a rule, once psychiatric symptoms appeared in a <tips=17>Type B</tips>, full recovery was impossible. Their extraordinary physical abilities also meant that any ward housing them required special equipment.

Japanese: 社会復帰のためのトレーニングも行われるが、職員の努力の甲斐なく、ほとんどの場合生活能力は回復しない。
English: Training for reintegration into society was provided, but despite the staff’s efforts, patients almost never recovered the ability to manage daily life.

Japanese: ルール的には家族が望めば退院は可能だが、症状の重い患者を家庭で暮らさせるのは不可能だ。家族にいくら深い愛情があってもだ。そして、すぐに病院に舞い戻るか、何か不幸な事件を起こしてしまうのが現実だった。
English: Under the rules, a patient could be discharged if the family wished. In reality, a severely ill patient could not live at home, no matter how deeply the family loved them. They would soon return to the hospital—or else some tragedy would occur.

Japanese: つまり、この病院に送られた患者は、そのほとんどが一生病院の敷地から一歩も出ることがなく生涯を終える。症状を改善させることも出来ぬまま。
English: In other words, most patients sent to this hospital would live out their lives without ever setting foot beyond its grounds. Their symptoms never improving.

Japanese: これが、この病院が収容所と呼ばれる所以であった。
English: That was why the hospital was called an internment center.

Japanese: このような施設は日本に何カ所かあり、いずれもなんらかの隠語で呼称されている。
English: There were several such facilities in Japan, and every one of them was known by some euphemism or code name.

Japanese: <tips=9>Y地区</tips>では発症後も街で生活するケースは少なくないが、それ以外の一般的な地域では、発症した<tips=17>タイプB</tips>のほとんどがどこかの施設に収容され、そこで一生を過ごすことになる。
English: In <tips=9>Y District</tips>, it was not uncommon for people to remain in the town even after symptoms appeared. In more ordinary parts of the country, however, nearly every <tips=17>Type B</tips> who developed symptoms was confined to an institution and spent the rest of their life there.

Japanese: どこも病床は余っており、軽度の患者でも預かり先に困ることはない。
English: All of these hospitals had beds to spare, so even patients with mild symptoms had no trouble finding somewhere to take them.

Japanese: 日本には病院が多すぎるのではないかと批判されている。
English: Japan was criticized for having too many hospitals.

Japanese: これらの病院は、<tips=17>タイプB</tips>自体の世間での悪いイメージと相まって、とてつもなく非人間的な施設だとイメージされている。
English: Coupled with the public’s prejudice against <tips=17>Type Bs</tips> themselves, these hospitals were widely imagined to be places of monstrous inhumanity.

Japanese: 看護師としての教育を受けた<tips=83>美紗</tips>でさえも、そのような偏見がなかったとは言えない。
English: Even <tips=83>Misa</tips>, with her training as a nurse, could not claim to have been free of such prejudice.

Japanese: 看護学校は、<tips=17>タイプB</tips>についてそこまで詳しく教えてはくれなかったし、最初に就職した病院では<tips=17>タイプB</tips>の患者を扱うことがなかった。
English: Nursing school had not taught her much about <tips=17>Type B</tips>, and at her first hospital she had never treated a <tips=17>Type B</tips> patient.

English: Handover at this hospital was interminable. What other hospital still used an antique like a Kardex these days? The building might be old, but surely the equipment and systems could still be replaced.

English: Apparently, time stopped for everything inside these walls. Tools, staff, patients—everything remained forever trapped in an earlier age. Was it because this was a public hospital?

English: Before the day staff, the colleague who had worked the night shift with her read aloud from the nursing record. The more carefully Misa tried to listen, the farther sleep carried her consciousness from reality.

English: One of the most experienced nurses on the ward, Maejima was forever interrupting other people’s reports this way. Her dedication was admirable. But once an impromptu conference began, handover ran long and the night staff got home late.

English: Those figures applied to the hospital as a whole. On the third floor of Ward B, there was only one male nurse, and only two of the nursing assistants were men.

English: Most male staff were assigned to wards with more violent patients. This chronic-care ward for women was given lower priority.

English: When they absolutely needed more male staff, they called another ward for help. But on this ward it was rare for a patient to become so agitated that no one could handle her.

English: Men were generally needed only for physical tasks: lifting a patient who remained lying down without moving into a wheelchair, or taking a carton full of documents down from a shelf. In practice, the women could handle almost every duty on their own.

English: T’s symptoms worsened periodically as though in response to the changing seasons, and ordinarily subsided just as quickly. This time, however, an episode had begun about a month earlier, and she had remained unwell ever since.

English: <tips=17>Type B</tips> episodes were often accompanied by auditory and visual hallucinations, and T experienced both.

Japanese: 元々自分でトイレに行って大便をするという能力に難のある患者だったのだが、それでも出来なくはなかった。しかし、今回のように具合が悪くなるとほとんど垂れ流し状態となり、しかも幻聴に指示されたと言って大便のついた下着で顔を拭いたりもする。
English: She had always had difficulty using the toilet to defecate, though she was not entirely incapable of it. When her condition worsened as it had now, she became almost completely incontinent. English: That was why, whenever her condition worsened, she was put in a coverall to prevent such unsanitary acts.

Japanese: こうした現場で扱われるツナギというのは、見た目は工務員などが着る上下が繋がったあの衣服と変わらない。違っているのは、ファスナーを開くには専用の金具が必要で、患者は自分で脱ぐことが出来ないという点だ。
English: The coveralls used in places like this looked no different from the one-piece work clothes worn by tradesmen. The difference was that opening the zipper required a special tool, so patients could not take them off by themselves.

English: It was a kind of restraint garment used for patients who habitually scratched at their bodies and for patients like T, who removed a diaper herself once it was soiled and fouled the ward.

English: Some time had passed since T was put in the coverall. She had settled down again and was complaining of auditory hallucinations less often.

English: If she remained in a coverall and diaper, she might completely lose what imperfect ability she had retained to use the toilet herself. Nurse Maejima was therefore proposing that it might be time to remove the coverall.

English: <tips=92>Nurse Mizumura</tips>, who was responsible for T, cautiously argued that it might still be too early. Another nurse said that T had repeated these unsanitary acts too many times: they should give up on preserving that ability and keep her in diapers.

Japanese: こうした意見の対立はくだらないように思われるかもしれないが、この病棟では重要なやりとりとされていた。
English: The disagreement might sound trivial, but on this ward it was an important discussion.

Japanese: 一度レベルが落ちた<tips=17>タイプＢ</tips>というものはもう回復しない。だから、B棟三階の入院患者の多くは退院を目的とはしていない。残された能力を、少しでも長く維持することが目的となっている。
English: Once a <tips=17>Type B’s</tips> level of functioning declined, it never recovered. Most patients on the third floor of Ward B were therefore not working toward discharge. The objective was to preserve their remaining abilities for as long as possible.

Japanese: このTの場合はトイレで排便出来る状態を保つのが目的だが、他の患者だと、入浴時に自分で体を洗うのを目的にしたり、与薬時にコップ一杯の水で薬を飲めるようになることを目指したりしている。
English: For T, the objective was to preserve her ability to defecate in the toilet. With other patients, the goal might be washing themselves at bath time or becoming able to take their medicine with a glass of water when it was dispensed.

Japanese: 急性病棟は少し事情が違う。人によっては退院を目指せる場合もあるし、暴力や危険行為といった抜き差しならない話題が主になったりするのだが、この慢性病棟では、こうした日々の細々としたことが話題の中心となる。そして、こういった話題に真剣になるのはスタッフの熱意の表れでもある。
English: An acute ward was somewhat different. Some patients there could work toward discharge, and discussion often centered on urgent matters such as violence or dangerous behavior. On this chronic ward, the small details of daily life took center stage. The staff’s willingness to treat those details seriously was itself a sign of their dedication.

Japanese: それは<tips=83>美紗</tips>だってわかってはいるが、何も朝の申し送り時にはやらなくても、というのが正直なところであった。
English: <tips=83>Misa</tips> understood that too. Honestly, though, did they really have to do it during morning handover?

English: As Misa saw it, the veteran nurses on this ward were much too attached to their patients. They treated them almost as if they were their own children.

English: R had suffered her first episode at fifteen and been hospitalized for the first time at eighteen. Nurse Fujiwara had been responsible for her ever since R was transferred here ten years earlier.

English: R’s condition had progressed far. Her intellect had severely deteriorated, and her delusions often led to disruptive behavior, making her a regular source of trouble on the ward. But perhaps the troublesome patients were the ones a nurse grew fondest of. R had her own peculiar charm as well.

English: Whenever R caused trouble, Nurse Fujiwara apologized to the other staff—“I’m sorry about my girl”—and gave R a stern scolding. R wilted every time. But her illness had robbed her of the ability to learn, and in the end she always did it again.

Japanese: Ｒは今年でもう五十九才になり、藤原ナースよりも年上だが、彼女のことを「お母さん」と呼んでいる。
English: R was now fifty-nine, older than Nurse Fujiwara, but called her ‘Mother.’

English: Repeated episodes had damaged R’s memory, and perhaps she could no longer tell the nurse apart from her real mother. If she did think of Fujiwara as her mother, she must have found her terribly nagging. Yet whenever R’s health declined or her delusions left her confused, Fujiwara noticed before anyone else and came to her aid. For a patient, she was probably the most dependable person in the world.

English: When the young <tips=83>Misa</tips> first encountered relationships like this between patients and nurses, she thought they went too far for a medical setting.

English: Once she began working on the ward herself, however, her view shifted. The patients here had almost no hope of recovery; they would only continue to decline, and they would spend every day remaining to them “living” in this place. Perhaps it was not an ordinary medical setting at all.

“What was that?”

English: The nurses’ station where they performed their duties was separated from the patients’ living space by a transparent sheet of durable acrylic, allowing an unobstructed view of the dayroom.

English: Had one patient attacked another? Violence was common on the men’s wards, but far less frequent here. When it did occur, it was usually directed not at other patients but at the staff who had to intervene during an episode of agitation.

Japanese: そのあざけりの態度に、<tips=1>亮</tips>は表情一つ変えず言葉を続ける。
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> continued without the slightest change of expression in the face of Liao’s mockery.

Japanese: 「<tips=81>龍頭</tips>の後見人となれば、格としては僕よりも上だし、あんたにとっては何も恥ずかしいことじゃない。もちろん、仕事は何もしなくて良い。……いや、この街ではもうどういった仕事をする必要もないんだ。あんたは第一線を退いて街の外で暮らすんだ。あんたの組織は執行部の管理下に入る」
English: “As guardian to the <tips=81>Longtou</tips>, you would outrank even me formally, so there is nothing shameful in it for you. Naturally, you need do no work at all. ...No, there will be no need for you to conduct any sort of business in this city again. You will retire from the front line and live outside the city. Your organization will come under the executive committee’s control.”

Japanese: 「私は街から追放で、組織は解体して<tips=69>義勝</tips>に吸収するということか」
English: “You mean to exile me from the city, dismantle my organization, and absorb it into <tips=69>Yisheng</tips>?”

Japanese: 薬が本来の効き目を発揮し、落ち着きを取り戻したのか、<tips=27>廖</tips>の顔つきには鋭さが戻る。
English: Perhaps the drug had begun to work as intended and restored his composure; the sharpness had returned to <tips=27>Liao’s</tips> face.

Japanese: 「馬鹿を言っちゃいけない」
English: “Do not talk such nonsense.”

Japanese: さすがにこういった場合の<tips=27>廖志明</tips>は迫力のある表情をするものだ。しかも、こんな絶望的な状況でも微塵もそれを感じさせない態度で、端で見ている林の背をぞくりとさせるものがあった。
English: <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips> could be genuinely intimidating at a moment like this. Even in so desperate a position, his manner betrayed none of it, and a chill ran down Hayashi’s back as he watched from the edge of the room.

Japanese: 林氏はこうした組織のボスというものを間近に見るのは初めてだったが、なるほど伊達ではないのだと不本意ながら納得せざるをえなかった。
English: Mr. Hayashi had never seen the head of an organization at such close range. Against his will, he understood that the man’s position was no empty title.

Japanese: が、最も近くで正面に座った<tips=1>亮</tips>は何も感じなかったようだ。
English: Yet <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips>, seated directly opposite Liao at closest range, appeared to Hayashi not to feel a thing.

Japanese: 「そうかな？　最大限の敬意を払っているんだがね」
English: “Is that so? I believe I am showing you the utmost respect.”

Japanese: 彼はさらりと言う。
English: He spoke lightly.

Japanese: 「僕はこのままあんたを始末したっていいんだ。罪状は<tips=39>ジェフリー</tips>の件だけで充分だしね。しかし、まがりなりにもあんたは初代……つまり僕の父の若き日の恩人であり、長年にわたって最大の協力者でもあった。だからこうして、特別な厚遇を用意したんだ」
English: “I could dispose of you right now. The charges in the <tips=39>Jeffrey</tips> affair alone would be enough. But whatever else may be said of you, you were a benefactor to the first Longtou—my father—in his youth, and his foremost ally for many years. That is why I’ve arranged this exceptionally generous treatment for you.”

Japanese: 「ふん、わかったわかった。こうなっては是非もなし。後見人になってやるから、もう帰ってくれ。早く治療をしなくては、おれは失血で死んでしまう」
English: “Hmph. Very well, very well. There is nothing to be done now. I will become your guardian, so go home. Unless I receive treatment quickly, I will bleed to death.”

Japanese: そして<tips=27>廖</tips>は、シッシッと、手を振って犬でも追い払うような仕草をする。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> waved his hand as though shooing away a dog.

Japanese: それに対して<tips=1>亮</tips>は、胸元から携帯端末を取り出すと、指先で操作をし、その画面を<tips=27>廖</tips>に見えるように置く。
English: In response, <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> took a mobile device from inside his coat, worked the controls with his fingertips, and placed the screen where <tips=27>Liao</tips> could see it.

Japanese: その画面には生体認証を促すメッセージが表示されている。
English: A message on the screen requested biometric authentication.

Japanese: <tips=27>廖志明</tips>が親指を画面に押し当て、口頭で暗証番号を言えば、銀行のメニューに入り、手続きが行えるというものだ。
English: If <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips> pressed his thumb to the screen and spoke his PIN aloud, the device would open the banking menu and allow the necessary procedures.

Japanese: 「承諾するのなら、あんたの個人資産をこちらの管理下に置かせて貰う。すべてが終わったら返還する」
English: “If you accept, I will place your personal assets under our control. They will be returned once everything is over.”

Japanese: 差し出された画面を前に、<tips=27>廖</tips>は口ごもる。
English: Faced with the screen waiting for his authentication, <tips=27>Liao</tips> faltered.

Japanese: 「はやくしてくれないか？　失血死がこわいんだろう？」
English: “Would you hurry? You are frightened of bleeding to death, aren’t you?”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>が促すのに、<tips=27>廖</tips>は苦笑し、
English: At <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> prompting, <tips=27>Liao</tips> gave a strained smile.

Japanese: 「そんなことをしなくても大丈夫。私は嘘をついたりはしないよ」
English: “There is no need for that. I would never tell a lie.”

Japanese: 「どうしても認証したくないんだね？」
English: “So you absolutely refuse to authenticate?”

Japanese: 「この<tips=27>廖志明</tips>を信じろと言っている」
English: “I’m telling you to trust <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips>.”

Japanese: 「そうか」
English: “I see.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>はあっさりと端末を引っ込め、
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> simply withdrew the device.

Japanese: 「こんな状況でも従わないあんたの度胸に個人的には敬服するが、まあ客観的には賢明とは言えないね」
English: “Personally, I admire the nerve it takes to defy us even now. Objectively, however, I cannot call it wise.”

Japanese: 「ふざけるなっ！　だれが組織を手放して隠居などするか！」
English: “Do not mock me! Who would surrender his organization and retire?”

Japanese: 突然<tips=27>廖</tips>は吼えた。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> suddenly roared.

Japanese: 目の前で大声をあげられた<tips=1>亮</tips>は顔を顰め、
English: With Liao shouting in his face, <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> frowned and said,

Japanese: 「うるさいな」
English: “You’re loud.”

Japanese: 「殺すなら殺せ！　そうなれば私の組織とお前たちは全面戦争になるだろう。勝てると思うなよ。そもそも、私を殺してここから無事に帰れるかどうか……」
English: “Kill me if you mean to! If you do, my organization and yours will be plunged into all-out war. Do not imagine you can win. To begin with, even if you kill me, do you truly think you can leave here alive...?”

Japanese: 「あんたをここで殺したって、大した争いにはならないよ。……あんたは本当に、自分の部下が、自分の死後も戦ってくれると思っているのかい？」
English: “Killing you here would hardly lead to any serious conflict. ...Do you truly believe your subordinates would keep fighting even after you were dead?”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>はあきれたように溜息をつく。
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> sighed in exasperation.

Japanese: 「あんたの組織は確かに巨大だが、僕らと争いたがっているのはあんただけだ。あんたが死んだら、僕は<tips=39>ジェフリー</tips>の件を公表し、組織の掟通りの処罰をしたことを宣言してから、きみの幹部たちに交渉をもちかける。すべてがすべてとは言わないが、大半はこちらの要求に応じてくれるだろう。我々と戦うより協力した方が利益になるのは彼らにもすぐ理解出来る。……あんたが知っているとおり、あんたの部下はみな非常に優秀で合理的で賢明だ。無意味な抗争よりビジネスを優先するだろうね」
English: “Your organization is certainly enormous, but you are the only one in it who wants to fight us. If you die, I will make the <tips=39>Jeffrey</tips> affair public, announce that you were punished according to the organization’s rules, and then open negotiations with your senior men. I won’t claim that every one of them will agree, but most will accept our terms. They will quickly understand that cooperating with us is more profitable than fighting us. ...As you know, your subordinates are all extremely capable, rational, and prudent. They will put business before a pointless war.”

Japanese: <tips=27>廖</tips>は反論をせずに、睨み付けている。ここで言い返さないということは、彼もその態度とは裏腹に<tips=1>亮</tips>と同じ見解を持っているということだろう。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> offered no rebuttal and merely glared. His failure to answer suggested that, whatever his defiant manner, he shared <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> assessment.

Japanese: 「だからあんたが本当に僕らに勝つつもりだったら、自分の身だけは最優先で守るべきだったのさ。くだらない女遊びは自重してね。……僕らの方から手を出すはずがないと、なめてたのかな？　僕らが、もっとあんたたちのことを恐れていると思っていた？　……その辺はやっぱり、結局ただの商売人上がりで、弱いモノを相手に暴力を使ってきた甘えなんだろうね。市民を脅しながら生きてきたあんたは、組織同士の戦いをしたことがない。市民だったら<tips=74>廖ファミリー</tips>の名前に怯えて何も出来ないだろうが、僕らはそうじゃない」
English: “If you truly intended to defeat us, you should have made protecting yourself your first priority and restrained yourself from this foolish womanizing. ...Did you underestimate us because you thought we would never strike first? Did you think we were more afraid of you than that? ...In the end, I suppose that is the complacency of a mere merchant who has used violence only against the weak. You have spent your life threatening ordinary citizens. You have never waged war against another organization. A citizen may be too frightened by the name <tips=74>Liao Family</tips> to do anything, but we are not.”

Japanese: 淡々と語る<tips=1>亮</tips>を、<tips=27>廖</tips>はあざ笑い、
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> sneered at <tips=1>Tse Leung’s</tips> dispassionate speech.

Japanese: 「わかったようなことを。ボスというものはそうじゃない。ビクビク怯えて女遊びも出来なくなれば、部下たちも侮るだろう。お前の父親だって、いくら命を狙われたって平然とレストランに飯を食いに行っていたよ」
English: “You talk as if you understand. That isn’t how a boss behaves. If he cowers in fear until he can’t even go womanizing, his subordinates will despise him. Even your father would calmly go out to restaurants no matter how many people were trying to kill him.”

Japanese: 「あんたの場合、その結果がこのみじめな有様なんだから、考え方を改めた方がいいな」
English: “In your case, since that way of thinking has left you in this miserable state, you’d better reconsider it.”

Japanese: 「この世界に生きている以上、誰だって最期はみじめなものさ。私はどんな死に方だろうが、恥だとも失敗だとも思わん」
English: “Anyone who lives in this world meets a wretched end. However I die, I will consider it neither shame nor failure.”

Japanese: <tips=27>廖</tips>は虚勢を張って笑って見せる。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> forced a laugh in a show of bravado.

Japanese: 「まあ何でも良いさ。とにかく、重要なのはビジネスだ。あんたは引退を拒否したが、やはりそれは間違っている」
English: “Whatever. What matters is business. You refused to retire, but that remains the wrong choice.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>は机に置かれたままの<tips=81>龍頭</tips>の杯を見つめながら話している。
English: As he spoke, <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> kept his eyes on the <tips=81>Longtou’s</tips> cup, still sitting on the table.

Japanese: 林氏はなぜ彼がこの交渉の場面でまったく相手の顔を見ようとしないのか、不自然に思ったが、理由を思いつくよりも早く<tips=1>亮</tips>は次の言葉を口にする。
English: Mr. Hayashi found it unnatural that <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> would not look at the other man’s face at all during the negotiations, but before he could think of a reason, Tse Leung spoke again.

Japanese: 「戦争になれば誰も得をしない。やはり、円満解決を目指そうじゃないか」
English: “No one profits from a war. Let us aim for an amicable settlement after all.”

Japanese: 「銃弾で傷つけ、脅迫をしながら円満解決とは笑わせてくれる」
English: “You shoot and threaten me, then speak of an amicable resolution. How very amusing.”

Japanese: 「<tips=27>廖志明</tips>、拗ねてる場合じゃない。いまからあんたはご自慢の頭脳で正しい判断を下さなければならないんだ。なに、難しいことじゃない。あんたの両肩に乗っているそいつがスイカか何かじゃないのならば、すぐにわかるはずさ」
English: “<tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips>, this is no time to sulk. You now have to use that vaunted intellect of yours to make the correct decision. It isn’t difficult. If the thing sitting on your shoulders isn’t a watermelon or something, the answer should be obvious.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>は相変わらず視線を相手に向けない。
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> still would not look at the other man.

Japanese: 「あんたは優秀だったが、もう終わった人間だ。もっとも、もし<tips=81>龍頭</tips>になっていても、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>のメンバーは誰もついて来なかったろうけどね。いくつかのファミリーが<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>を去り、そしてあんたは弱体化した<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>を立て直すことは出来ない。だけれど、僕と僕の仲間ならそれが出来る」
English: “You were a capable man, but your time is over. Though even if you had become <tips=81>Longtou</tips>, no member of <tips=7>YS</tips> would have followed you. Some Families would leave <tips=7>YS</tips>, and you would be unable to rebuild the weakened <tips=7>YS</tips>. But my companions and I can.”

Japanese: <tips=27>廖</tips>は何も言わずににらみ返している。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> said nothing, only glaring back at him.

Japanese: 「あんたにチャンスをやろうと言っているんだ。僕はあんたの組織を吸収したら、その後は、他のファミリーも取り込むつもりだ。大体、一つの組織のなかで、香港人だの、客家人だの、ブラジル人だの、いくつものファミリーに別れているのは効率的ではないんだよ。くだらない分断がなくなれば、<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>はもっと強くて巨大な組織になる」
English: “I’m offering you a chance. Once I absorb your organization, I intend to take in the other Families as well. In the first place, it is inefficient for Hong Kong people, Hakka people, Brazilians, and all the rest to be divided into separate Families within a single organization. Once those pointless divisions are gone, <tips=7>YS</tips> will become larger and stronger.”

Japanese: 「そう上手くいくと思うなよ」
English: “Do not imagine it will go so smoothly.”

Japanese: <tips=27>廖</tips>は吐き捨てるように言う。
English: <tips=27>Liao</tips> spat the words.

Japanese: 「いくさ」
English: “War.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>は目を細め、
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> narrowed his eyes.

Japanese: 「すべてのファミリ－は一旦解散して、新しい<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の部下となる。その時には、もちろん、<tips=76>香港派</tips>というのも消えてなくなっているし、<tips=69>義勝</tips>なんていう古くさい名前を口にするやつもいないだろう。今の執行部も潰すんだ。このやりかたなら、きっとうまくいく」
English: “Every Family will first dissolve, and its members will become subordinates of a new <tips=7>YS</tips>. Naturally, by then the <tips=76>Hong Kong faction</tips> will also have ceased to exist, and no one will utter an antiquated name like <tips=69>Yisheng</tips>. The present executive committee will be dissolved as well. This approach is sure to work.”

Japanese: そう言った時、<tips=25>世傑</tips>も驚きの目で<tips=1>亮</tips>を見た。
English: When he said this, even <tips=25>Sai-kit</tips> looked at <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> in surprise.

Japanese: 彼も事前に知らされていない内容だったのだろう。
English: Evidently, he too had not been informed of the plan beforehand.

Japanese: 「新しい<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>は、出身地による派閥は作らせない」
English: “The new <tips=7>YS</tips> will permit no factions based on place of origin.”

Japanese: 「机上の空論だな。血と土地というものは人間の深い部分に根ざしたものだ。それはお前の父でも出来なかったことだ」
English: “An armchair fantasy. Blood and land are rooted deep within human beings. Not even your father could achieve that.”

Japanese: 「昔はそうだったのかもしれない。だけど、世代はかわる。僕らはこの街で生まれ育った。肌の色が違うやつらと遊んで育ち、家の中でしか母国の言葉を使わないやつも沢山いる。これからは、こういう人間がこの街を仕切ってゆくんだ。行ったこともない土地の名前に縛られるのは馬鹿馬鹿しい話さ」
English: “Perhaps that was true in the old days. But generations change. We were born and raised in this city. We grew up playing with people of other skin colors, and many of us use the language of our ancestral country only inside the home. From now on, people like us will run this city. It is absurd to be bound by the name of a land one has never even visited.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>は机の上の<tips=81>龍頭</tips>の杯の位置を少し右に動かし、
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> shifted the <tips=81>Longtou’s</tips> cup slightly to the right on the table and continued,

Japanese: 「そもそも街自体が古くさいのさ。元の国になんか戻れないような連中ばかりなのに、どうして国の名前を看板に掲げて争っているのか。全てを非効率にして、そしてその代償は自分たちが支払うんだ。……ウエスト通りの立ちんぼなんか悲惨だよ。元締めが稼ぎの七割くらい持って行く。何の商売の手伝いもしないくせに、上前だけはねてゆくんだ。<tips=59>暗闇通り</tips>で商売をしようにも、よその組織の縄張りで商売をすれば殺されても文句を言えない。そして売春婦たちは病気だの暴力だので、平均五年で死ぬ。育てられなかった子供はストリートチルドレンになるか、死んでその辺にゴミのように捨てられる。一方、穀潰しどもはその金で殺し合いをするんだ。こういう構造は街のあらゆるところに存在する。金貸しのあんたなら、こういう状況はよく知っているだろう？　故郷を捨てれば解決することなんだ。そして街が潤えば<tips=7>ＹＳ</tips>の力にもなる」
English: “The city itself is antiquated to begin with. It’s full of people who can never return to their countries of origin, so why do they hang those countries’ names on their signs and fight over them? It makes everything inefficient, and they themselves pay the price. ...The streetwalkers on West Street live miserably. Their handlers take around seventy percent of their earnings. They do nothing to help the business, yet skim their cut off the top. If the women try to work on <tips=59>Darkness Street</tips>, they’re doing business in another organization’s territory and can hardly complain if they’re killed. The prostitutes die after an average of five years, from disease or violence. Children they cannot raise become street children—or die and are discarded nearby like garbage. Meanwhile, the parasites use that money to kill one another. This same structure exists throughout the city. As a moneylender, you know these conditions perfectly well, don’t you? Abandoning the old homelands would solve the problem. And if the city prospers, <tips=7>YS</tips> grows stronger with it.”

Japanese: 「くだらん話だ」
English: “What nonsense.”

Japanese: <tips=27>廖</tips>は不快を隠しもせずに顔を歪め、
English: <tips=27>Liao’s</tips> face twisted with undisguised displeasure.

Japanese: 「……お前は私を撃って、茶飲み話をしに来たのか？　だとすればイカしたジョークだな！　くどくどと無駄話をするくらいなら、私を殺してみろ！　そして、お前が言うように、私の部下が降伏するか、試してみれば良い。さあ殺せ！　その後に、お前も死ぬことになるのだからな！」
English: “...Did you shoot me merely to come and have a pleasant chat? If so, that’s one hell of a joke! Rather than drone on with idle talk, try killing me! Then see whether my subordinates surrender as you claim. Go on, kill me! You’ll die afterward in any case!”

Japanese: そう吐き捨てて相手の顔を睨み付ける。
English: He spat out the words and glared into his opponent’s face.

Japanese: 「あまりがっかりさせないで欲しいもんだ。どうしても僕らに季節外れのスイカジュースを作らせたいのかい？」
English: “I do wish you wouldn’t disappoint me so. Are you really determined to make us serve up watermelon juice out of season?”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>は肩をすくめて溜息をつくと、
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> shrugged and sighed, then said,

Japanese: 「……仕方ない。次はきみと話そうか。<tips=28>トーマス・リャオ</tips>」
English: “...It can’t be helped. Shall I speak with you next, <tips=28>Thomas Liao</tips>?”

Japanese: 「<tips=28>トミー</tips>だって？」
English: “<tips=28>Tommy</tips>?”

Japanese: 声をあげたのは、<tips=27>廖志明</tips>だ。
English: The cry came from <tips=27>Liao Chi-ming</tips>.

Japanese: 「そうとも」
English: “That’s right.”

Japanese: <tips=1>亮</tips>はこともなげに答える。
English: <tips=1>Tse Leung</tips> answered as though it were the most ordinary thing in the world.

Japanese: 「おい小僧。<tips=28>トミー</tips>がこの部屋にいるというのか？」
English: “Hey, kid. Are you saying <tips=28>Tommy</tips> is in this room?”
